docs.title: ACE3P Documentation
docs.text:
ACE3P (Advanced Computational Electromagnetic 3D Parallel) is a suite of parallel finite-element codes developed at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory for the design and analysis of particle accelerator components. It solves Maxwell's equations and coupled multiphysics problems on unstructured tetrahedral meshes with high-order basis functions, and runs on HPC systems using MPI.

  • Getting started

    Get a NERSC account, connect to Perlmutter with a ThinLinc desktop, and run your first job. Cubit and ParaView are already installed there.

    Getting started

  • Cubit

    Geometry and meshing for ACE3P: the pillbox walkthrough, journal files, sidesets and blocks, mesh quality.

    Cubit chapter

  • Workflow

    The common ACE3P pipeline: geometry and meshing in Cubit, mesh conversion with acdtool, solving, and post-processing.

    Workflow overview

  • Modules

    User guides and tutorials for each solver: Omega3P, S3P, T3P, Track3P, Pic3P, TEM3P, and Gun3P.

    Module guides

  • Reference

    Input-file keyword tables generated directly from the ACE3P source, so they always match the released code.

    Keyword reference

docs.title: Solver modules
docs.text: Module Domain Typical use Omega3P Frequency domain, eigenmodes Cavity resonant modes, Q factors, R/Q, mode damping with couplers S3P Frequency domain, driven S-parameters of couplers, waveguides, and multi-port structures T3P Time domain Wakefields, transient response, beam-driven fields Track3P Particle tracking Multipacting, dark current, field emission Pic3P Particle-in-cell Self-consistent beam dynamics with space charge TEM3P Multiphysics Thermal and mechanical analysis coupled to RF fields Gun3P Electrostatic / beam optics Electron guns, space-charge-limited emission acdtool Utility Mesh conversion and statistics, RF post-processing, field extraction

docs.title: About these docs
docs.text:
This site replaces the CW23 workshop slide decks that were distributed as PDFs. The content is organized as a manual rather than as lecture notes, it is searchable, and it is versioned alongside ACE3P releases. Use the version selector in the header to view documentation for a specific release.

The keyword reference pages are regenerated from the ACE3P source tree whenever a release is tagged, and the Releases section carries the developers' notes for each one. See Contributing for how that works and how to propose changes.

Citing ACE3P

Please cite ACE3P when publishing results obtained with it. Contact the development team at ace3p@slac.stanford.edu.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: This documentation is maintained in the public slaclab/ace3p-docs repository and published at https://slaclab.github.io/ace3p-docs/. Anyone can read it and file issues; changes go through pull requests and are merged by the ACE3P team.

docs.title: Report a problem
docs.text: Use the Edit this page icon at the top of any page to open the source on GitHub, or open an issue at https://github.com/slaclab/ace3p-docs/issues. Include the page URL and, for technical errors, the ACE3P version you observed the behavior with.

docs.title: Build locally
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:slaclab/ace3p-docs.git
cd ace3p-docs
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The site rebuilds on every save. Run mkdocs build --strict before pushing; it fails on broken links and missing pages, which is also what continuous integration checks.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
docs/
  index.md              home page
  getting-started/      system setup: S3DF, Perlmutter, local tools
  workflow/             the common pipeline: input format, mesh, batch jobs
  modules/              one guide per solver; omega3p/ has tutorials
  reference/            GENERATED keyword tables, do not edit by hand
  interfaces/           GUI, dashboard, workflow assistant
  assets/               images, grouped by module
tools/
  extract_keywords.py   generates docs/reference/*.md from ACE3P source
mkdocs.yml              navigation and theme

Add a new page by creating the Markdown file and adding it to nav in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Writing guidelines
docs.text:
• Write prose, not slide bullets. Each tutorial step says what to do, what to expect, and why.
  • Show real input files from the examples directory, complete and runnable. Annotate with comments rather than paraphrasing.
  • Use system-neutral commands in module guides. Put S3DF and Perlmutter specifics in Getting Started.
  • Images go in docs/assets/<module>/ and are referenced with relative paths.
  • Do not commit credentials, personal home-directory paths, or unpublished results.

docs.title: Regenerating the reference pages
docs.text:
The reference tables come from the ACE3P source tree:

python tools/extract_keywords.py /path/to/ace3p --out docs/reference

The script scans for Get(kvc, "Keyword", InitOrFallback<T>(default) ...), the find, findSwitch, and findContainer calls, and the string-compare parser of the rf post-processor. Point it at a checkout of the tagged ACE3P release so that the revision recorded in each page matches the tag.

docs.title: Documentation written with the code
docs.text:
ACE3P developers can document a feature in the same pull request that implements it, in docs/user/ of the ACE3P source repository (see its README.md). Two kinds of page are picked up:

  • docs/user/<module>/<topic>.md appears here under Modules > (module) > Notes from the source tree, carrying a banner that names its origin.
  • docs/user/CHANGES/<tag>.md or CHANGES/next.md becomes the release-notes page under Releases.

tools/assemble_source_docs.py does the copying and rewrites the generated part of the navigation. Pages copied this way are owned by the ACE3P repository: edit them there, not here, or the next release overwrites the change.

docs.title: What happens at an ACE3P release
docs.text:
The ACE3P source repository has a workflow, .github/workflows/docs-keywords.yml, that runs when a release tag v* is pushed:

  1. Regenerates the keyword tables and copies the developer pages.
  2. Builds the site strictly, so a broken link in a developer page fails before anything is published.
  3. Opens a pull request here on branch release-docs/<tag> and requests auto-merge.
  4. When the pull request has merged, tags this repository <tag>. The deploy workflow then publishes that version and points latest at it.

For this to run unattended, the ACE3P repository needs the secret ACE3P_DOCS_TOKEN (a token with contents and pull-request write access here), and this repository needs Allow auto-merge enabled in Settings and a branch ruleset on main requiring the build check. Without auto-merge the pull request waits for a maintainer; the workflow still tags once it is merged within 30 minutes, and otherwise the tag is made by hand as below.

Hand-written guides and tutorials are never changed by this workflow. Only docs/reference/*.md, docs/modules/*/from-source/, docs/releases/, and the generated block of mkdocs.yml are.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Documentation versions are published with mike. Pushing to main updates the dev version. Pushing a tag vX.Y publishes that version and points the latest alias at it:

git tag v2026.10
git push origin v2026.10

Tag the documentation with the same version string as the ACE3P release it describes. The ACE3P binaries print that string in their start-up banner as ACE3P Release: v2026.10, so a user can match a run to its documentation version.

docs.title: Cubit: geometry and meshing for ACE3P
docs.text:
Cubit is the geometry and mesh generation toolkit from Sandia National Laboratories that every ACE3P workflow starts with. It is installed on Perlmutter and S3DF (see where to run Cubit), so you can follow this chapter in a remote desktop without installing anything. This chapter walks through building and meshing a pillbox cavity, first interactively so you learn the interface, then as journal files so the process is reproducible. The export rules and the acdtool conversion that follow are on the mesh preparation page.

Cubit's own tutorials at cubit.sandia.gov and coreform.com go deeper on the tool itself.

docs.title: The interface
docs.text:
Cubit on first launch. Model Tree at left, graphics window center, Command Panel at right, Command Line at bottom. Close the Tip of the Day.

Five regions matter:

Region Use Model Tree Browse volumes, surfaces, curves, and the sidesets and blocks you define. Clicking an entity highlights it in the graphics window. Graphics window Rotate with the left mouse button, zoom with the right, pan with the middle. Click an entity to select it; its ID appears in the command line. Command Panel Three rows of icons: Mode (Geometry, Mesh, Exodus for boundary conditions, and so on), then Entity (Volume, Surface, Curve, Vertex), then Action. Each click descends one level and ends at a form with an Apply button. Command Line Every GUI action echoes here as a text command. You can also type commands directly. The History tab keeps the last hundred. Type help <command> for syntax. Properties Page and Power Tools Properties of the selected entity; geometry checking and repair tools.

Set the working directory before anything else, with File, then Set Directory, or by typing cd "/path/to/pillbox" in the command line. Files are read and written relative to it.

Work in millimeters, export in meters

Build and mesh in the natural units of the drawing, usually millimeters, to avoid tolerance problems with tiny coordinates. Scale by 0.001 as the last step before export. ACE3P expects meters.

docs.title: Modeling a pillbox interactively
docs.text: The target is an L-band pillbox: cavity 90 mm long and 100 mm in radius, beam pipe 35 mm in radius and 300 mm long overall, iris rounded with a 12 mm radius. Its TM010 mode is near 1.2 GHz.

docs.title: Create the cell
docs.text:
In the Command Panel choose Mode Geometry, Entity Volume, Action Create, select Cylinder, enter height 90 and radius 100, and click Apply. The command line shows the equivalent text:

create cylinder height 90 radius 100

docs.title: Add the beam pipe
docs.text: Repeat with height 300 and radius 35. Both cylinders are centered on the origin along z, so the pipe passes through the cell.

docs.title: Unite
docs.text:
Under Entity Volume, Action Boolean, pick Unite, enter volume IDs 1 2, Apply. Then compress ids so the surviving body is volume 1 with consecutive surface and curve numbers:

unite volume 1 2
compress ids

The three Boolean operations are Unite, Subtract, and Intersect. Cubit renumbers entities after every Boolean or deletion, and the gaps confuse later commands, so get in the habit of compressing IDs immediately.

docs.title: Round the iris
docs.text:
Click a curve in the graphics window and its ID appears in the command line. The two iris circles where the pipe meets the cell are curves 5 and 6 after the compress. Under Entity Curve, Action Modify, choose Blend/Chamfer, enter 5 6, Blend, radius 12, Apply:

modify curve 5 6 blend radius 12

The full model. The command line records every step taken through the GUI, which is what you will collect into a journal file.

docs.title: Cut to a quarter
docs.text:
Omega3P needs only the symmetric quarter. Entity Volume, Action Webcut, Coordinate Plane, volume 1, YZ plane, offset 0, Apply, then delete the half you do not want:

webcut volume 1 with plane xplane offset 0 noimprint nomerge
delete volume 2
compress ids
webcut volume 1 with plane yplane offset 0 noimprint nomerge
delete volume 1
compress ids

Which half to delete depends on which side of the plane Cubit numbered as volume 2; check the Model Tree or click the body. Webcutting also has cylindrical, extended-surface, and tool-body variants for more complex cuts.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
File, Export, choose ACIS .sat, name it pillbox, Export All, Finish:

export acis "pillbox.sat" overwrite

ACIS is Cubit's native solid format and preserves exact geometry. Keep the .sat file; it is the input to the meshing step and to any later modification.

docs.title: The same model as a journal file
docs.text:
Every command above is in the Command Line's Command tab. Tools, then Journal Editor, then File, Import, Command Tab pulls them into an editor. Clean up, parameterize, and save as step1-Make-pillbox.jou:

step1-Make-pillbox.jou
reset

#{cav_length = 90}
#{cav_radius = 100}
#{bp_length  = 300}
#{bp_radius  = 35}
#{iris_rounding = 12}

create Cylinder height {cav_length} radius {cav_radius}
create Cylinder height {bp_length} radius {bp_radius}
unite volume 1 2
compress ids
modify curve 6 5 blend radius {iris_rounding}

webcut volume 1 with plane xplane offset 0 noimprint nomerge
delete volume 2
compress ids
webcut volume 1 with plane yplane offset 0 noimprint nomerge
delete volume 1
compress ids

export acis "pillbox.sat" overwrite

Three edits turn a transcript into a reusable script:

  • reset at the top clears the session so the journal gives the same result every time.
  • #{name = value} variables replace literal numbers, so a dimension changes in one place. Expressions like {0.5*cav_length} are allowed.
  • overwrite on the export so replaying does not stop at a prompt.

Play it with the Play Journal File toolbar button, or from the Journal Editor, or by typing playback "step1-Make-pillbox.jou". The Journal Editor can also play a selection: highlight lines, right-click, Play Selected. That is the way to debug a journal step by step.

Entity IDs are not stable across Cubit versions or geometry changes

modify curve 5 6 works because of how Cubit numbered the curves after this particular unite. Change a dimension, reorder operations, or move to a different Cubit release and the iris curves may be 7 and 8. When a journal fails at a blend or sideset command, click the entity in the graphics window to find its current ID. Cubit's journal idless on mode records commands by coordinates instead of IDs and avoids the problem at the cost of readability.

docs.title: Meshing
docs.text:
ACE3P uses quadratic tetrahedral elements, tetra10, whose mid-edge nodes follow curved surfaces. The meshing journal imports the .sat, sets the scheme, chooses a size, meshes, assigns sidesets and blocks, scales, and exports.

step2-Mesh-pillbox.jou
reset
import acis "pillbox.sat"

volume all scheme tetmesh
volume 1 sizing function type skeleton min_size 3 max_size 12
mesh volume 1

# 1 and 2: beam pipe ends, 3 and 4: symmetry planes
sideset 1 surface 2
sideset 2 surface 4
sideset 3 surface 3
sideset 4 surface 1
sideset 6 surface all except 2 4 3 1

block 1 volume all
block 1 element type tetra10

volume 1 scale 0.001
export genesis "pillbox.gen" overwrite

quality vol all distortion high 0.0 draw mesh

Open it in the Journal Editor and play it line by line the first time so you can inspect each stage.

docs.title: Element size
docs.text:
Two choices:

UniformAdaptive (skeleton sizing) 
volume 1 size 10
mesh volume 1

Every element about 10 mm. Simple and predictable. Generate meshes at several sizes and run a convergence study.

volume 1 sizing function type skeleton min_size 3 max_size 12 max_gradient 1.2 scale 5
mesh volume 1

Element size follows local geometry: fine at the iris rounding, coarse along the pipe. Parameters:

Argument Range and default Effect min_size, max_size auto Bounds on edge length in model units max_gradient 1.0 to 3.0, default 1.5 How fast size may change between neighbors. Smaller gives smoother transitions and more elements. scale 1 to 10, default 7 Overall density. Smaller is finer. time_accuracy_level 1 to 3, default 2 Internal effort of the sizing function. Try higher levels only if the mesh is poor.

To try a different size, delete the mesh first: delete mesh volume 1, or Mode Mesh, Entity Volume, Action Delete in the panel.

docs.title: Sidesets and blocks
docs.text:
A sideset groups surfaces and becomes a boundary ID in ACE3P. A block groups volumes and becomes a material attribute. Both are set under Mode Exodus in the Command Panel, or by command:

sideset 1 surface 2
block 1 volume all

Find surface IDs by clicking in the graphics window. The idiom sideset 6 surface all except 2 4 3 1 assigns every surface not already named to the wall, so nothing is left without a boundary ID. The command line confirms what each sideset received:

Check the assignment visually with draw sideset 1 2 3 4, which shows only those surfaces:

For models with many surfaces, Cubit groups make sideset assignment robust. See the window example in the S3P tutorials and the two-mesh models in the TEM3P tutorials, which select surfaces by coordinate and by merge status:

group "sym1" add surface with x_coord < 0.001
group "ms"   add surface with is_merged

docs.title: Quality check in Cubit
docs.text: The last line of the journal, quality vol all distortion high 0.0 draw mesh, colors elements by distortion. Reading "No mesh elements in range" in the command line means none are badly distorted. The definitive check is acdtool meshconvert on the HPC side, described on the mesh preparation page.

docs.title: Tips for harder models
docs.text:
• Check and heal imported CAD first. Power Tools has geometry diagnostics; import acis "file.sat" heal repairs common defects. Small sliver surfaces and short curves are the usual meshing failures.
  • Imprint and merge multi-volume models before meshing: imprint body all then merge body all. Without merging, touching volumes have duplicate faces and the mesh is disconnected. The lossy load tutorial shows the consequence.
  • Mesh small or critical surfaces first with their own size, then the volume: surface 14 size 0.5 then mesh surface 14 then mesh volume 3. The BPM example in the T3P tutorials does this for a button face.
  • Split a volume to control size regionally. Webcut a volume into pieces, give each its own sizing function, and merge. The TTF3 coupler in the TEM3P example separates five materials this way.
  • Smooth the transition from fine to coarse regions with max_gradient near 1.2. Abrupt size changes degrade element quality and the finite-element solution.
  • Periodic faces need identical meshes. Mesh the master face, copy it to the slave with copy mesh surface ... onto surface ..., then mesh the volume without smoothing. The periodic boundary tutorial shows the commands.
  • Start coarse. A quick coarse mesh reveals sideset mistakes and geometry problems before you invest in a fine one.

docs.title: When acdtool reports bad elements
docs.text:
If acdtool meshconvert finds invalid second-order tetrahedra, it replaces them with straight-sided ones and writes a warning. If it finds elements with poor aspect ratio or shape measure, it writes .vtu files marking them. Load the .ncdf through the SLAC toolbar in ParaView, then File, Open the .vtu, color it red, and make the mesh translucent to see where to refine.

Invalid elements, in red, clustered where a curved surface meets a flat one at a sharp angle. Finer min_size or a blend on the edge fixes this.

docs.title: Where to run Cubit
docs.text:
Cubit is installed on both HPC systems, so you do not need your own copy. Launch the GUI from a ThinLinc desktop on Perlmutter, or from a NoMachine desktop on S3DF. Details, including how to install Cubit on your own computer if you prefer, are on the tools page.

A journal can also be played with no display, which is what an automated workflow does. On S3DF:

/sdf/group/rfar/software/Cubit-16.12/cubit -batch -nographics -input step2-Mesh-pillbox.jou

The ACE3P GUI and lume-ace3p chain batch meshing with the solvers this way.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
ACE3P solvers run on an HPC system under the Slurm batch scheduler. The main platform is NERSC Perlmutter, where ACE3P is installed for all users with access to the m349 allocation. Pre-processing (geometry and meshing in Cubit) and post-processing (ParaView) are already installed on Perlmutter as well, so a complete workflow needs nothing more than a NERSC account and a remote-desktop client.

S3DF is for SLAC users only

SLAC's Shared Scientific Data Facility (S3DF) also hosts ACE3P, Cubit and ParaView, but it is only reachable with a SLAC account. If you are at SLAC, see Running on S3DF. Everything else in this manual applies to both systems.

flowchart LR
    subgraph HPC["Perlmutter (or S3DF)"]
        direction LR
        A[Cubit<br/>geometry + mesh] --> B[acdtool meshconvert] --> C[Solver<br/>omega3p, s3p, ...] --> D[acdtool postprocess]
        C --> E[ParaView<br/>visualization]
    end
    L[Your laptop<br/>ThinLinc client] -. remote desktop .-> HPC

docs.title: Three steps to a first run
docs.text:
1. Get access. Request a NERSC account on the m349 project through the ACE3P team (ace3p@slac.stanford.edu) and set up multi-factor authentication at iris.nersc.gov. NERSC's own guide is at docs.nersc.gov/accounts.
  2. Connect with a graphical desktop. Install the ThinLinc client and connect to Perlmutter. You get a Linux desktop with a terminal, Cubit and ParaView in one window. See Connecting with ThinLinc below.
  3. Run the pillbox example. Follow Running on NERSC Perlmutter to load the ACE3P environment and submit a job, then the Omega3P pillbox tutorial.

Once a job has run, the Workflow chapter explains the five-step pipeline every solver follows, and the Cubit chapter covers geometry and meshing in depth.

docs.title: Connecting with ThinLinc
docs.text:
ThinLinc gives you a full Linux desktop on Perlmutter in a window on your laptop. It is the recommended way to work with ACE3P because Cubit and ParaView are graphical programs, and running them on Perlmutter avoids copying meshes and field files back and forth.

  1. Install the client for your operating system from cendio.com/thinlinc/download. Windows, macOS and Linux are supported.
  2. Create an sshproxy key. ThinLinc at NERSC authenticates with a key generated by sshproxy, not with a password. Follow the sshproxy section on the Perlmutter page once; the key is valid for 24 hours.
  3. Connect. In the ThinLinc client set the server to thinlinc.nersc.gov, your NERSC username, and under Options, Security choose Public key with the path to the nersc key from sshproxy. On first connection compare the fingerprint with the one published by NERSC.
  4. Open a terminal from the desktop menu. You are on a Perlmutter login node; everything on the Perlmutter page applies.

NERSC's full guide, including troubleshooting, is at docs.nersc.gov/connect/thinlinc.

Plain SSH still works

If you only need a terminal, ssh <username>@perlmutter.nersc.gov is enough. You will then run Cubit and ParaView on your own computer; see Pre- and post-processing tools.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Familiarity with a Unix shell: cd, ls, cp, mkdir, and a text editor such as vi, emacs, or nano.
  • For the SSH route, an SSH client. Linux and macOS have ssh and scp built in. On Windows 10 or later use ssh from PowerShell, or install PuTTY and WinSCP.

docs.title: Example files
docs.text:
The tutorials use the examples and exercises prepared for the CW23 workshop. They are installed on both systems:

System Examples Exercises Perlmutter $CFS/ace3p/cw23/examples $CFS/ace3p/cw23/exercises S3DF /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/cw23/examples /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/cw23/exercises

Each cw23/ tree also holds the per-module command references in commands/, the ParaView macros in macros/, and release notes in news/. Copy the directory you need into your own working area before running anything; the example directories are read-only.

docs.title: Running on NERSC Perlmutter
docs.text: Perlmutter is NERSC's flagship system. ACE3P is installed in the ace3p project directory on the Community File System (CFS) and currently runs on the CPU nodes. Each CPU node has two AMD EPYC 7763 processors, 128 cores in total, and 512 GB of memory.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
The recommended way to work is through a ThinLinc remote desktop, which gives you a terminal, Cubit and ParaView in one window on Perlmutter. Setup is described on the Getting started page. ThinLinc needs an sshproxy key, so do the sshproxy step below first.

For a terminal only:

ssh <username>@perlmutter.nersc.gov

Enter your password followed immediately by your six-digit one-time password, with no space between them.

docs.title: Avoid repeated OTP prompts with sshproxy
docs.text:
NERSC provides sshproxy to generate a key that is valid for 24 hours.

Linux and macOSWindows 
scp <username>@dtn01.nersc.gov:/global/cfs/cdirs/mfa/NERSC-MFA/sshproxy.sh .
./sshproxy.sh -u <username>
ssh -l <username> -i ~/.ssh/nersc perlmutter.nersc.gov

scp <username>@dtn01.nersc.gov:/global/cfs/cdirs/mfa/NERSC-MFA/sshproxy.exe .
.\sshproxy.exe -u <username> --format openssh -o nersc
ssh -l <username> -i nersc perlmutter.nersc.gov

For PuTTY or WinSCP, omit --format openssh to get a .ppk key.

docs.title: Load the ACE3P environment
docs.text:
cp $CFS/ace3p/perlmutter/CPU/perlmutter-ace3p.sh ~/
source ~/perlmutter-ace3p.sh

The ACE3P binaries live in $CFS/ace3p/perlmutter/CPU/. $CFS expands to /global/cfs/cdirs.

docs.title: Cubit and ParaView
docs.text: Both are installed on Perlmutter and run in a ThinLinc desktop, so meshes and results never have to leave the system. See Pre- and post-processing tools for how to start them and for the ParaView SLAC toolbar.

docs.title: Working directory
docs.text:
Run jobs from scratch, not from your home directory:

mkdir -p $SCRATCH/ace3p
ln -s $SCRATCH/ace3p ~/ace3p
cd ~/ace3p

docs.title: Transfer files
docs.text:
Use the data transfer nodes dtn01 through dtn04:

# laptop -> Perlmutter
scp pillbox4.gen <username>@dtn01.nersc.gov:ace3p/pillbox/
# Perlmutter -> laptop
scp '<username>@dtn01.nersc.gov:ace3p/pillbox/omega3p_results/*.mod' .

Windows users can do the same in WinSCP with protocol SCP, host dtn01.nersc.gov, port 22.

docs.title: A minimal batch script
docs.text:
run-omega3p.batch
#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH -C cpu
#SBATCH -q debug
#SBATCH -A m349
#SBATCH -N 1
#SBATCH -t 00:10:00
#SBATCH -J omega3p
#SBATCH -e ace3p.e%j
#SBATCH -o ace3p.o%j

srun -n 16 -c 16 --cpu-bind=cores $CFS/ace3p/perlmutter/CPU/omega3p pillbox.omega3p
Line Meaning -C cpu Request CPU nodes -q debug Short test queue, 30 minute limit. Use regular for production. -A m349 The ACE3P allocation -n 16 -c 16 16 MPI ranks, 16 cores each, filling one 128-core node 
sbatch run-omega3p.batch
squeue -u $USER       # or: sqs
scancel <jobid>
tail -f ace3p.o<jobid>

See the NERSC job documentation for queue policies and more options. Track3P runs best with few ranks and OpenMP threads; its batch script is in Batch jobs.

docs.title: Running on S3DF
docs.text:
SLAC users only

S3DF, SLAC's Shared Scientific Data Facility, is reachable only with a SLAC computing account. Users elsewhere should use NERSC Perlmutter, which is the main ACE3P platform. The rest of this manual applies to both systems.

ACE3P is installed under the rfar group area and runs on the milano partition. Cubit and ParaView are installed as well; see Pre- and post-processing tools.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
ssh <username>@s3dflogin.slac.stanford.edu

Login nodes are for editing and job submission only. Do not run solvers on them.

docs.title: Load the ACE3P environment
docs.text:
Source the environment script once per session. It loads the matching OpenMPI module and puts the ACE3P binaries on your PATH.

source /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/ace3p.sh
which omega3p acdtool

Tip

Add the source line to your ~/.bashrc if you use ACE3P regularly.

docs.title: Partitions and accounts
docs.text:
Setting Value Notes Partition milano AMD Milan nodes, 128 cores per node Account rfar:regular Replace rfar with your own allocation if different QOS normal Non-preemptable; use preemptable for lower-priority throughput

Check your allocations with sacctmgr show assoc user=$USER format=account,partition,qos.

docs.title: A minimal batch script
docs.text:
run-omega3p.sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --partition=milano
#SBATCH --account=rfar:regular
#SBATCH --qos=normal
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=16
#SBATCH --time=00:30:00
#SBATCH --job-name=omega3p
#SBATCH --output=%x.%j.out
#SBATCH --error=%x.%j.err

source /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/ace3p.sh
srun --overlap --cpu-bind=none -n 16 omega3p pillbox.omega3p

Submit, monitor, and cancel with the usual Slurm commands:

sbatch run-omega3p.sh
squeue -u $USER
scancel <jobid>

docs.title: Interactive sessions
docs.text:
For short tests, allocate an interactive shell on a compute node:

srun --partition=milano --account=rfar:regular -n 16 --time=01:00:00 --pty /bin/bash
source /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/ace3p.sh
mpirun -n 16 omega3p pillbox.omega3p

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Location Use $HOME Scripts and small inputs. Quota is limited. /sdf/group/rfar/<user> Project space for inputs and results. /sdf/scratch/<group>/<user> Large temporary output. Purged periodically.

Temporary files

Some ACE3P tools write scratch files to $TMPDIR. If /lscratch on a node is full, set export TMPDIR=/sdf/scratch/<group>/<user>/tmp before running.

docs.title: Hybrid MPI and OpenMP (Track3P)
docs.text:
Track3P is OpenMP-parallel inside each MPI rank, and every rank holds the whole mesh, so it runs best with few ranks and many threads. Request one or two ranks per node and let OpenMP fill the cores:

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=16
srun -n 1 -c 16 track3p input.track3p

Complete S3DF and Perlmutter batch scripts for the hybrid layout are in Batch jobs. The field solvers (Omega3P, S3P, T3P, TEM3P) are pure MPI; run them with one rank per core.

docs.title: Pre- and post-processing tools: Cubit and ParaView
docs.text:
Two graphical programs bracket every ACE3P run: Cubit builds the geometry and the mesh before the solver, and ParaView displays the fields and particles after it. Both are installed on Perlmutter and on S3DF. You do not need to install them yourself; run them in a remote desktop on the HPC system, next to your meshes and results.

Cubit ParaView Role Pre-processing: geometry, meshing, sidesets and blocks, .gen export Post-processing: fields, modes, particle trajectories, wake plots On Perlmutter Cubit 16.16 under $CFS/ace3p/tools/, run in a ThinLinc desktop ParaView 5.11.0 under $CFS/ace3p/tools/, run in a ThinLinc desktop; NERSC client-server mode for large data On S3DF Installed, run in a NoMachine desktop or with ssh -X Installed, run in a NoMachine desktop or through the web visualizer On your own computer Possible; needs a license Possible; free download Learn more Cubit chapter Omega3P tutorial, module pages

docs.title: Cubit
docs.text:
Cubit from Sandia National Laboratories is the geometry and meshing tool used throughout the ACE3P workflow. ACE3P drives it mostly through journal files (.jou), scripts of Cubit commands that make a mesh reproducible. The Cubit chapter walks through building and meshing a pillbox cavity, first interactively, then by journal, and ends with the export rules. The short version:

export Genesis "model4.gen" block all overwrite

Mesh elements must be quadratic tetrahedra (tetra10) and the model must be scaled to meters before export. See Mesh preparation.

docs.title: Cubit on Perlmutter
docs.text:
Cubit 16.16 is installed in the ACE3P project area. Connect with ThinLinc, open a terminal and start it:

$CFS/ace3p/tools/Cubit-16.16/cubit &

The GUI opens on the ThinLinc desktop. Set the working directory to your scratch area (File, then Set Directory) so the .gen file lands where acdtool meshconvert will read it.

docs.title: Cubit on S3DF
docs.text:
Cubit 16.12 is installed at /sdf/group/rfar/software/Cubit-16.12/. Start it from a NoMachine desktop or an ssh -X session:

/sdf/group/rfar/software/Cubit-16.12/cubit &

A journal can also be played with no display, which is what automated workflows do:

/sdf/group/rfar/software/Cubit-16.12/cubit -batch -nographics -input step2-Mesh-pillbox.jou

docs.title: Installing Cubit on your own computer
docs.text:
Cubit requires a license. Two routes:

  • Sandia Cubit is free for U.S. government use: government agencies and laboratories, and companies working under a direct U.S. government contract. Request a license through the ASC software request form; approval takes a few weeks. Downloads and the licensing rules are at cubit.sandia.gov/licensing and cubit.sandia.gov/downloads.
  • Coreform Cubit is the commercial version for everyone else, with trial and academic licenses from coreform.com. Journal files written for one run in the other.

The tutorials were written with Cubit 16.x. Running Cubit locally means copying .gen files up to the HPC system with scp.

docs.title: ParaView
docs.text: ParaView is free, open-source software from Kitware. ACE3P results are read through the SLAC toolbar, a plugin shipped with every ParaView release, which loads a mesh (.ncdf) together with mode or field files (.mod) in one step.

docs.title: ParaView on Perlmutter
docs.text:
ParaView 5.11.0 with the SLAC toolbar is installed in the ACE3P project area. In a ThinLinc desktop:

$CFS/ace3p/tools/ParaView-5.11.0-MPI-Linux-Python3.9-x86_64/bin/paraview &

This is the version the tutorials and the CW23 macros were tested with. NERSC also provides newer ParaView releases (5.12 and later) and a client-server mode for very large datasets, where the GUI runs on your computer and the data stays on Perlmutter. Setup is in the NERSC ParaView guide; the client version must match the server version listed there.

docs.title: ParaView on S3DF
docs.text: ParaView 5.11.1 is installed at /sdf/group/rfar/software/ParaView-5.11.1-MPI-Linux-Python3.9-x86_64/. Start bin/paraview from a NoMachine desktop.

docs.title: Installing ParaView on your own computer
docs.text: Download the installer for Windows, macOS or Linux from paraview.org/download. No license is needed. Use version 5.11 or later; the SLAC toolbar is included. Running ParaView locally means copying .ncdf and .mod files down from the HPC system with scp.

docs.title: Enable the SLAC toolbar
docs.text:
Do this once per ParaView installation, on the HPC system or your laptop:

  1. Open Tools, then Manage Plugins.
  2. Select SLACTools and click Load Selected.
  3. Expand the entry and check Auto Load so it is active on every start.

A SLAC button appears in the toolbar. Click it, pick the .ncdf mesh and the .mod field file, and the model loads with the field data attached.

docs.title: Load the ACE3P macros
docs.text:
The CW23 materials include Python macros for common ACE3P plots. Add each one through Macros, then Add new macro:

Macro Used with Purpose nextmode.py Omega3P, S3P, T3P, TEM3P Step through modes or time steps enhancement.py Track3P Plot the enhancement counter resonant_lineplot.py, resonant_location.py Track3P Resonant particles: energy vs field level, impact locations trajectory.py Track3P Animate particle trajectories wakeplot.py T3P Plot wake potentials timeFFT.py T3P FFT of a time signal

The macros are in $CFS/ace3p/cw23/macros on Perlmutter and /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/cw23/macros on S3DF. If you run ParaView on your laptop, copy that directory down first.

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text:
The command line is the primary way to run ACE3P, and everything in this documentation can be done from a terminal. The ACE3P GUI is a desktop application built around the same solvers and input files: it writes the .omega3p, .s3p and other inputs described in this manual, submits the same binaries to Perlmutter, and adds a 3D field viewer and an AI assistant. Its own pages are at https://ace3p.slac.stanford.edu/user-interface.

Two Python toolkits drive ACE3P programmatically and are not yet documented here:

  • lume-ace3p, public on GitHub, wraps Cubit, acdtool, and the ACE3P solvers in the LUME interface for design parameter scans.
  • A3PI, the ACE3P-IMPACT integration, chains Cubit, Omega3P, acdtool field extraction, and the IMPACT-T beam dynamics code under libEnsemble for gun optimization. Its user guide and an example are in the commands/ and examples/a3pi/ directories of the CW23 materials.

Learning the input format in this manual carries over to all of them.

docs.title: ACE3P GUI
docs.text:
The ACE3P GUI is a desktop application that builds input files for all seven solvers, meshes geometries, submits jobs to NERSC Perlmutter, and post-processes the results, without editing text files by hand. It is developed by the ACE3P team and released separately from the solvers. The current version is 1.4.15.

Everything about the GUI is on its own pages:

  • Overview and downloads: https://ace3p.slac.stanford.edu/user-interface
  • User guide: https://mothmanslac.github.io/ace3p-gui-docs/, with sections on getting started, a tutorial, simulation setup, running jobs, workflow orchestration, result post-processing, the AI assistant, and a reference.

This manual does not repeat that material. It documents the input files, keywords and command-line tools that the GUI produces and calls, so the two fit together: use the GUI to build a run, and this manual to understand what each field means.

docs.title: Getting the GUI
docs.text:
PerlmutterWindows or Linux desktop

Already installed in the ACE3P project area. Connect with a ThinLinc desktop, open a terminal and run:

/global/cfs/cdirs/ace3p/gui/ACE3P-GUI-v1.4.15-linux-x86_64/ACE3P-GUI

Download ACE3P-GUI-v1.4.15-windows-x86_64.exe or ACE3P-GUI-v1.4.15-linux-x86_64.tar.gz from the link on the user-interface page. No installer is needed; unpack and run. The GUI connects to Perlmutter to submit jobs, so you still need a NERSC account.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Area In the GUI In this manual Simulation setup Forms that write the .omega3p, .s3p, .t3p, .track3p, .tem3p, .gun3p input as you type Input file format, command syntax and keyword tables Meshing Drives Cubit journals and acdtool meshconvert Cubit, Mesh preparation Running jobs Submits to Perlmutter and monitors the queue Running on Perlmutter, Batch jobs Workflow orchestration Parameter sweeps and optimization chains Module pages describe the individual steps Post-processing 3D field viewer, data explorer, acdtool postprocess Omega3P post-processing and the module pages AI assistant Troubleshooting and input help inside the GUI

Questions and feedback on the GUI go to the ACE3P team at ace3p@slac.stanford.edu.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
ACE3P is a family of solvers that share one mesh format, one input syntax, and one post-processing toolchain. Each module addresses a different physics regime.

Module Guide Status of this documentation Omega3P User guide and tutorials Complete: concepts, three tutorials, post-processing S3P User guide and tutorials Complete: concepts, input blocks, output files, three tutorials T3P User guide and tutorials Complete: wakefields, port excitation, moving window, SIBC, five tutorials Track3P User guide and tutorials Complete: multipacting and dark current, six tutorials, S3DF rerun Pic3P User guide and tutorial Complete: self-consistent PIC, LCLS gun tutorial TEM3P User guide and tutorials Complete: thermal, elastic, LF detuning, mechanical eigenmodes, four tutorials Gun3P User guide and tutorial Complete: DC gun iteration, sheet beam gun tutorial with MICHELLE comparison

docs.title: Which module do I need?
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Q1{What do you want?} 
    Q1 -->|Resonant frequencies, Q, R/Q, field patterns| O[Omega3P]
    Q1 -->|Transmission and reflection vs frequency| S[S3P]
    Q1 -->|Wakefields or transient beam-driven fields| T[T3P]
    Q1 -->|Multipacting or dark current| TR[Track3P]
    Q1 -->|Self-consistent beam with space charge| P[Pic3P]
    Q1 -->|Heating, stress, or frequency shift from deformation| TE[TEM3P]
    Q1 -->|Electron gun or DC beam optics| G[Gun3P]

Several modules chain together. Track3P reads the mode fields that Omega3P produces. TEM3P reads Omega3P or S3P fields as a heat source. The ACE3P GUI and lume-ace3p automate such chains.

docs.title: Gun3P
docs.text: Gun3P is a static solver for DC electron guns. It computes the electrostatic potential from the electrode voltages, emits electrons from the cathode under the space-charge limit, tracks them, deposits their charge, and iterates until the fields and the beam are self-consistent. Optionally it also solves the magnetostatic field of the beam's own current. The outputs are the emitted current, the beam trajectories and envelope, emittances at a screen, and the fields on the mesh.

docs.title: What it solves
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    I["Initialize"] --> E["Electrostatic solve<br/>∇·(ε∇φ) = −ρ"]
    E --> M["Magnetostatic solve<br/>∇×(μ⁻¹∇×A) = J<br/>(optional)"]
    M --> T["Emit at cathode,<br/>track particles,<br/>deposit ρ and J"]
    T --> C{"Converged?<br/>or max iterations"}
    C -- no --> E
    C -- yes --> P["Post-process:<br/>fields, trajectories,<br/>screen emittance"]

The electrostatic field is \(\mathbf{E} = -\nabla\phi\) with Dirichlet conditions on metal surfaces (fixed voltage) and Neumann on symmetry planes. The optional magnetostatic field is \(\mathbf{B} = \nabla\times\mathbf{A}\) driven by the beam current. Particles obey \(d\mathbf{p}/dt = q(\mathbf{E} + \mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B})\). The cathode emits according to the Child-Langmuir space-charge-limited law, with the current determined by the local field a short distance in front of the surface, so emission and field settle together.

Convergence is measured as the relative change in the field degrees of freedom between iterations, and the run stops when it drops below the tolerance or when MaxIterations is reached. Current and perveance per iteration are printed so you can see the approach to steady state.

Electron trajectories in a sheet beam klystron gun, colored by momentum, with the focusing electrode and anode.

Benchmark. Gun3P was compared with the commercial code MICHELLE on this gun: both give 129.3 A of emitted current with cathode current densities of 1.75 to 2.4 A/cm², from different mesh types.

docs.title: Input file
docs.text:
Every block and key is described in the Gun3P command syntax.

A .gun3p file has up to four top-level blocks. It shares the ElectrostaticProblem and MagnetostaticProblem block types with TEM3P, and the Tracker block with Track3P; the syntax conventions of each carry over.

dcgun.gun3p (abridged)
DCGunProblem: {
  RunId: test
  SymmetryFactor: 1                   // 1 full, 2 half, 4 quarter
  ElectricRelativeTolerance:  1.00e-12
  ElectricRelativeTolerance2: 1.00e-12  // with magnetic solver active
  MagneticRelativeTolerance:  1.00e-12
  MaxIterations: 32
  Save iteration data: On
}

ElectrostaticProblem: {
  AnodeBoundaryId: 12
  MeshFile: dcgun.ncdf
  BasisOrder: 2
  CurvedSurfaces: on
  Charge averaging factor: 0.1        // under-relaxation of the deposited charge

  VolumeMaterial: {
    Id: 1
    MediumName: Vacuum
    PhysicalParameter: { Name: Permittivity  ConstantValue: 1. }
  }

  Write dofs to disk: on
  Use reduced solver: On
  Outputs: { Dofs for vizualization: On }

  Boundary: { Id: 1   ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 0. }       // cathode
  Boundary: { Id: 2   ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: -500. }    // focus electrode
  Boundary: { Id: 12  ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 115000. }  // anode
  Boundary: { Id: 3   ConditionType: Neumann    NeumannValue: 0. }         // open boundary
  Boundary: { Id: 10  ConditionType: Neumann    NeumannValue: 0. }
  Boundary: { Id: 4   ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 0. }

  Compute non zero initial guess: On
  LinearSolver: {
    Solver: CG                        // or MUMPSFLOAT for small problems
    Preconditioner: CHOLESKY
    Tolerance: 1.00e-16
    MaxIterations: 5000
  }
}

MagnetostaticProblem: {
  ...same mesh, materials, and solver pattern; all boundaries Dirichlet 0...
}

Tracker: {
  JobName: ./gun3p_results/OUTPUT
  Particlefile: partpath
  t: 6.0e-6                           // forward tracking time, s
  Generate output for vizualization: on
  Print emission statistics: On
  Backward: { t: 6.0e-6  Generate output for vizualization: on }

  Domain: {
    t0: 0.0
    dt: 1.0e-12
    MaxImpacts: 2
    Emission Nx: 200   Emission Ny: 100   Emission Nz: 300
    Tracking Nx: 200   Tracking Ny: 100   Tracking Nz: 300
    Tracking box x min: -0.11   Tracking box x max: 0.11
    Tracking box y min: -0.04   Tracking box y max: 0.04
    Tracking box z min: -0.001  Tracking box z max: 0.18
  }

  Monitor: {
    Type: PlaneCrossingsVsT
    Name: screen
    Plane point: 0., 0., 0.15999
    Plane normal: 0., 0., 1.
    Compute densities: On
    Max x for densities: 0.110   X number of densities: 11
    Max y for densities: 0.004   Y number of densities: 80
  }

  MeshInterface: { Type: pd  Localizer: { Type: USS_Curve } }

  Emitter: {
    Type: 6                           // Child-Langmuir
    BoundaryID: 1                     // cathode sideset
    N: 1.0e+0                         // electrons per macroparticle
    M: 9.10938e-31                    // kg
    Q: -1.60218e-19                   // C
    d: 0.1e-3                         // macroparticle radius, m
    Sample Type: 1                    // 1 face centers, 2 stochastic
    Child Langmuir: {
      Whole boundary is emitter: On
      Use electric field direction for initial forward velocity: On
      Max allowed total current: 1.35e+9
      Reference z for emission surface: 1.50e-3
      Particles per face: 5
      ...tuning parameters, keep the defaults...
    }
  }

  Material: { BoundarySurfaceID: 1   Type: 2 }   // 2 = Absorber
  Material: { BoundarySurfaceID: 2   Type: 2 }
  Material: { BoundarySurfaceID: 12  Type: 2 }
  ...
}

docs.title: DCGunProblem
docs.text: Key Meaning RunId Label for the run SymmetryFactor 1, 2, or 4. Emitted current is scaled to the full gun. ElectricRelativeTolerance Convergence criterion on the electric field change between iterations, when the magnetic solver is off ElectricRelativeTolerance2, MagneticRelativeTolerance The same when the magnetic solver is on MaxIterations Stop here regardless. The example uses 32; convergence to 10⁻⁵ relative change takes about that many. FirstIterationForMagnetostaticProblem Iteration at which to start including the beam's self-magnetic field. Leave commented out to never run it. JustGenerateTreecotree Run on one core to precompute the tree-cotree gauge for the magnetostatic solve. Needed if the magnetostatic problem fails to converge. Save iteration data Keep per-iteration fields and particles under OUTPUT/ITER_<n>/

docs.title: ElectrostaticProblem and MagnetostaticProblem
docs.text:
These follow the TEM3P conventions: MeshFile, BasisOrder, CurvedSurfaces, one Boundary block per sideset, VolumeMaterial by block. Differences:

Key Meaning AnodeBoundaryId Sideset of the anode. Used to reference the accelerating voltage for perveance. Charge averaging factor Under-relaxation: new charge = (1 − f) × previous + f × computed. 0.1 is stable; larger converges faster if it converges. VolumeMaterial.PhysicalParameter Name is Permittivity, Permeability, or Sigma, with ConstantValue Compute non zero initial guess Start each iteration's solve from the previous solution Use reduced solver Eliminate constrained DOFs before solving. Keep on. Outputs.Dofs for vizualization Write the field for gun3pOutputConverter to turn into a .mod file Outputs.ElectrostaticFieldToken, FileName, Nx, Ny, Nz Also export the field on a Cartesian grid, for use as an external field in Track3P Outputs.XRange, YRange, ZRange Optional, two values each (min max, metres). Extent of that grid per axis; an axis not given spans the mesh bounding box. Points outside the mesh are written as zero. Added in the October 2026 release. LinearSolver.Solver CG with CHOLESKY for large problems, MUMPSFLOAT for small. Other keys as shown.

In the magnetostatic problem every boundary is Dirichlet 0 and the material parameter is still named Permittivity in the examples, which the code accepts.

docs.title: Tracker
docs.text: Key Meaning JobName Output directory; must match the second argument on the command line t Forward tracking time in s. Make it long enough for the slowest particles to reach the screen. Backward Backward tracking from the emission reference plane to the cathode, used by the Child-Langmuir model to set the launch conditions Domain.dt Tracking time step Domain.Emission Nx/Ny/Nz, Tracking Nx/Ny/Nz Grid resolution for the particle localizer in the emission region and the tracking region Domain.Tracking box ... Bounding box of the tracking region, m. Particles outside are dropped. MeshInterface Localizer settings. Keep as in the example.

docs.title: Emitter
docs.text:
Type: 6 is Child-Langmuir, the model for thermionic DC guns. The other numbered types are shared with Track3P and are listed on its module page.

Key Meaning BoundaryID Cathode sideset N, M, Q Electrons per macroparticle, and the real particle mass and charge d Macroparticle radius for space-charge deposition Sample Type 1 launches from face centers, 2 stochastically across each face Child Langmuir.Reference z for emission surface Distance in front of the cathode at which the field is sampled to set the emission current Child Langmuir.Particles per face Macroparticles launched per cathode face per iteration. Increase for smoother current; the reference says to experiment for convergence. Child Langmuir.Max allowed total current Safety cap in μA

The remaining Child-Langmuir keys control the iteration strategy and are documented as "keep as default" in the command reference.

docs.title: Monitor
docs.text: Type Keys Output PlaneCrossingsVsT Plane point, Plane normal, Compute densities, density grid extents and counts Emittances and current density of particles crossing one plane, printed per iteration PlanesCrossing First plane point, Common plane normal, Distance between first and last planes, Number of planes The same at a stack of parallel planes

docs.title: Material
docs.text: Particle boundary behavior by sideset, numbered: 1 Reflector, 2 Absorber, 3 Secondary emitter, 4 Test surface, 5 SymmetryPlane. In a gun, every metal surface is an absorber.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
srun -n 256 gun3p dcgun.gun3p gun3p_results

The second argument names the results directory and must agree with Tracker.JobName. The sheet beam gun with 459,000 elements and 32 iterations took 232 s on 256 ranks across two nodes. Each iteration is a full electrostatic solve plus tracking, so the cost scales with iteration count.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Location Content gun3p_results/gun3p.log Timing summary. The detailed iteration log goes to standard output, so keep the Slurm output file. Standard output Per iteration: ||E dofs - prev|| ... rel. tol., emitted current and perveance from the Child-Langmuir model, and the screen monitor's emittances OUTPUT/previousPerveanceAtIter<n> Micro-perveance after each iteration, one number per file OUTPUT/emissionMap<n> Emission current per cathode face OUTPUT/ITER_<n>/E/, PARTICLES/ Per-iteration fields and trajectories when Save iteration data is on OUTPUT/E/, OUTPUT/M/ Final electrostatic and magnetostatic DOFs; staticDofs.ncdf.mod appears after the converter runs OUTPUT/PARTICLES/partpath_ts<n>.ncdf Particle positions per time step of the final iteration, for animation

docs.title: Post-processing
docs.text:
The fields are stored as DOF vectors. Convert them to ParaView .mod files with the companion program:

gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p e        # electric field, final iteration
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p m        # magnetic field
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p e 30     # electric field at iteration 30

Output goes to OUTPUT/E/staticDofs.ncdf.mod and OUTPUT/M/. If ElectrostaticFieldToken was on, the converter also writes the field on the Cartesian grid as a text file, which Track3P reads through Domain.ElectroStaticFieldMap. The Track3P module page describes that coupling.

In ParaView, load the mesh with the .mod file for the field and the partpath_ts*.ncdf series for the trajectories.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text: Sheet beam klystron gun: a 115 kV DC gun with a focus electrode, run to self-consistency and compared with MICHELLE.

docs.title: Gun3P tutorial: sheet beam klystron gun
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/gun3p/LSBK

A DC gun for a sheet beam klystron: a wide, flat cathode at ground, a focus electrode at −500 V, and an anode at 115 kV. The beam exits through the anode aperture toward a screen 16 cm downstream. Gun3P finds the self-consistent emitted current and the beam shape at the screen.

The full-model mesh, and the electrostatic potential: anode (red, 115 kV), cathode and focus electrode (blue, near 0 V).

docs.title: Mesh from a STEP file
docs.text:
Unlike the other tutorials, this geometry arrives as a CAD STEP file rather than a Cubit journal. The journal imports and heals it, refines the cathode surfaces, meshes, and assigns sidesets by explicit surface lists.

dcgun.jou
reset
import step "SBK_3D.step" heal

surface 1 size 3                           # cathode
surface 47 size 3
volume all scheme tetmesh
vol 1 sizing function skeleton scale 3 min_size 0.1 max_size 7 max_gradient 1.3
mesh volume all

sideset 1 surface 1 47                     # cathode
sideset 2 surface 33 12 3 23 32 31 48 49 22 21 10 11   # focus electrode
sideset 3 surface 34                       # open boundary
sideset 4 surface 2 36
sideset 12 surface 4 5 6 7 8 9 13 14 15 16 17 18 19 20 24 25 26 27 28 29 30 35 37 38 40 41 42 43 44 45 46   # anode
sideset 10 surface 39                      # open boundary

block 1 volume 1
block all element type tetra10
volume all scale 0.001
export genesis "dcgun.gen" overwrite

import step ... heal repairs small CAD defects on import. The result is 459,206 elements with boundary IDs 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 12. Long explicit surface lists like the anode's are fragile; for your own models prefer Cubit groups selected by coordinate or by name, as the Cubit page describes.

The cathode, focus electrode, and anode nose. The mesh is refined at the cathode where emission is computed.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
The full file is shown on the module page. The decisions it encodes:

  • Full model, SymmetryFactor: 1. The gun is not symmetric enough in its CAD representation to cut.
  • Voltages. Cathode 0 V, focus electrode −500 V, anode 115 kV. The small negative bias on the focus electrode shapes the beam edge.
  • Both field solvers. MagnetostaticProblem is present, so the beam's self-magnetic field is included once FirstIterationForMagnetostaticProblem is reached. In the shipped file that key is commented out, so the magnetostatic solve is set up but never activated; the run is electrostatic only.
  • 32 iterations, with the fields and particles of each saved.
  • Screen at z = 0.15999 m, just before the exit boundary at 0.16, collecting emittances and current density on an 11 by 80 grid.
  • Child-Langmuir emission from the whole cathode, five macroparticles per face, each representing one electron, with a 0.1 mm space-charge radius.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
srun -n 256 gun3p dcgun.gun3p gun3p_results

The run completed in 232 s on 256 ranks. Standard output carries the iteration history; gun3p_results/gun3p.log has only the timing summary.

docs.title: Convergence
docs.text:
The emitted current and micro-perveance from the Child-Langmuir model, per iteration:

Iteration Emitted current (A) Micro-perveance (μA/V3/2) 0 562.6 7.21 1 475.1 7.21 2 370.1 9.70 8 124.1 8.39 16 127.5 4.04 24 128.4 3.18 31 128.4 3.29

The first guess, with no space charge in the field, over-emits by a factor of four. Space charge builds up over the first ten iterations and suppresses the emission to its self-consistent value of 128.4 A, after which the current is steady and only the field keeps refining. The relative change in the electric field falls from 2.4×10⁻³ at iteration 1 to 1.6×10⁻⁵ at iteration 31, far from the 10⁻¹² tolerance in the input, so the run ended on MaxIterations. That is normal: the tolerance in the shipped file is unreachable in double precision, and 10⁻⁵ is well converged for engineering purposes.

Total emitted current and relative field error against iteration, from the workshop slides. The current settles by iteration 12; the field continues to converge geometrically.

docs.title: Comparison with MICHELLE
docs.text:
The same gun was simulated with MICHELLE, a commercial finite-element gun code. From the published comparison:

Quantity Gun3P MICHELLE Elements 1,316,530 tetrahedra 1,073,000 hexahedra Basis order 2 1 Emitted current 129.3 A 129.3 A Cathode current density 1.75 to 2.36 A/cm² 1.75 to 2.40 A/cm² Beam hitting electrodes 0 % 0 % Run time 5.5 h on 48 cores 63.6 h on 1 core

The tutorial's coarser 459,000-element mesh gives 128.4 A, within 0.7 percent of the fine-mesh value.

docs.title: Post-process
docs.text:
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p e
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p m

writes OUTPUT/E/staticDofs.ncdf.mod and the magnetic equivalent. In ParaView, load dcgun.ncdf with that .mod file for the potential and field, and add the OUTPUT/PARTICLES/partpath_ts*.ncdf series to animate the beam from cathode to screen. The screen monitor's emittances are in the standard output, labelled plane monitor 'screen', in π mm·mrad.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
• Turn on the self-magnetic field. Uncomment FirstIterationForMagnetostaticProblem: 1 or set it to an iteration after the current has settled. For a 129 A beam the magnetic self-pinch is not negligible.
  • Trim the iterations. The current is converged by iteration 12. Set MaxIterations accordingly and halve the run time, or raise Charge averaging factor cautiously to converge in fewer.
  • Export the field for Track3P. Add ElectrostaticFieldToken: On with a FileName and Nx, Ny, Nz to Outputs, and XRange, YRange, ZRange if you want the grid to cover only the gun region (for this gun, XRange: -0.02 0.02, YRange: -0.01 0.01, ZRange: 0.0 0.10 puts 90 % of the points inside the mesh instead of 23 %); rerun the converter, and the Cartesian field file can be loaded in Track3P as a static field alongside an RF field. The Coax-StaticField example under examples/track3p does exactly this.
  • Electrostatic only. Remove the Tracker block and set MaxIterations: 0 to use Gun3P as a plain electrostatic solver for electrode design.

docs.title: Gun3P: notes from the source tree
docs.text:
Pages written by the ACE3P developers alongside the code, copied from docs/user/gun3p/ in the ACE3P repository at release v2026.11. They describe features as implemented and complement the Gun3P guide.

  • Structured-grid E-field export on a user-chosen region

docs.title: Structured-grid E-field export on a user-chosen region
docs.text:
From the ACE3P source tree

Written by the ACE3P developers in docs/user/gun3p/grid-output-region.md and copied here for release v2026.11 on 2026-10-28. Propose changes in the ACE3P repository, not on this page.

Applies to gun3pOutputConverter and to the identical code in kly3pOutputConverter. Added October 2026 (PR #240).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
gun3pOutputConverter <input>.gun3p e can export the electrostatic E field of a Gun3P solution on a Cartesian grid. Track3P reads that file back as ElectroStaticFieldMap (class FieldMap3D in slacsupport) to superimpose a DC gun field on an RF mode, for example in the Coax-StaticField Track3P example.

Until now the grid always spanned the full bounding box of the mesh. For a gun whose cathode and anode occupy a small fraction of the model, most of the Nx x Ny x Nz points landed outside the mesh and were written as zero, and the useful region was sampled coarsely. The Outputs block now accepts optional XRange, YRange, ZRange keys that set the grid extent per axis. Axes not given keep the bounding box, so existing inputs produce exactly the same file as before.

docs.title: What was wrong before
docs.text:
• The grid extent was hard-wired to the mesh bounding box (DM_StatisticsManager::boundingBox). The only user control was the point count.
  • For the LSBK sheet-beam gun (model 44 x 44 x 18 cm, gun region about 4 x 2 x 10 cm) a 12 x 12 x 20 grid put 77 % of its points outside the mesh.
  • A missing Ny wrote its default into nx instead of ny, so ny stayed uninitialised.
  • The Nz fallback message said 50 while the code used 100.

docs.title: Input syntax
docs.text:
The keys live in the Outputs block of ElectrostaticProblem (for e) or MagnetostaticProblem (for m), next to the existing export keys.

ElectrostaticProblem: {
  ...
  Outputs: {
    Dofs for vizualization: On      // needed by the converter in any case
    ElectrostaticFieldToken: On     // turn the grid export on
    FileName: efield.txt            // written as gun3p_results/OUTPUT/E/<FileName>
    Nx: 50                          // points along x over the chosen region
    Ny: 50
    Nz: 200
    XRange: -0.02  0.02             // optional, metres, min max
    YRange: -0.01  0.01             // optional
    ZRange:  0.0   0.10             // optional
  }
}
Key Type Default Meaning ElectrostaticFieldToken On/Off Off Enable the grid export FileName string test.txt Output name under gun3p_results/OUTPUT/E/ Nx, Ny, Nz int 50, 50, 100 Grid points per axis over the region. A value of 1 is raised to 2. XRange, YRange, ZRange two doubles mesh bounding box Grid extent per axis, min max, metres. Independent per axis.

Rules:

  • A range may be smaller or larger than the mesh. Points outside the mesh are written as zero field, as before. FieldMap3D::FieldCartesian also returns zero outside the map, so Track3P behaviour is continuous either way.
  • Exactly two values per range key. One or three values abort with XRange must have exactly two values (min max), found N. Exiting...
  • min must be less than max, else XRange: min must be less than max (got 0.02 -0.02). Exiting...
  • The region in use is echoed once: output grid region: x [-0.02, 0.02] y [-0.01, 0.01] z [0, 0.1]

Run the converter as before, on one or more ranks:

mpirun -n 1 gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p e

docs.title: Output format (unchanged)
docs.text:
Three header lines, then one line per grid point with x varying fastest, then y, then z. Values are Ex Ey Ez in V/m.

<xmin> <xmax> <Nx>
<ymin> <ymax> <Ny>
<zmin> <zmax> <Nz>
<Ex> <Ey> <Ez>
...

The header now carries the chosen region rather than the bounding box, which is what FieldMap3D uses to place the map, so no change is needed on the Track3P side.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The grid section of outputConverter.C builds a LocalizerCurved over the local mesh, then for each grid point finds the containing tetrahedron and interpolates the node-averaged field vectField_av linearly inside it. The change only replaces the x1..z2 extents, taken from the bounding box, with the user values when a range key is present; the localization and interpolation are untouched. That is why a ranged grid whose points coincide with points of another grid gives identical values (see the validation).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Reproducible test: gun3p/testsuites-new/grid-region/run.sh (see its README). It uses the converged electrostatic DOFs of the CW23 LSBK example (/sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/cw23/examples/gun3p/LSBK, 421 714 tetrahedra, basis order 2), so no gun3p solve is needed. Five converter runs, then check.py:

Case Grid Checks full (no range keys) 12 x 12 x 20 over the bounding box header equals the bounding box in the log; 2880 rows rangeA x +-0.02, y +-0.01, z 0 to 0.10 m, 11 x 11 x 21 header equals the requested ranges; 2541 rows rangeB same x, y; z 0 to 0.05 m, 11 x 11 x 11 every point coincides with a rangeA point; field identical there bad_reversed XRange: 0.02 -0.02 aborts with the min/max message bad_single XRange: 0.02 aborts with the two-values message

Result on 2026-10-26, converter built from commit 9db95cc83: 15 checks, 0 failures.

Quantity full box rangeA points inside the mesh 22.9 % 90.5 % max abs E 7.1e6 V/m 3.0e6 V/m rangeA vs rangeB at coincident points max difference 0.0

A trilinear interpolation of the full-box grid onto the rangeA points differs from rangeA by tens of percent. That is expected: the full-box spacing is 4 cm in x and y on a gun a few centimetres across, so the coarse grid cannot represent the field there. It is the reason the region keys are useful.

docs.title: Files changed
docs.text:
• gun3p/src/outputConverter.C: range keys, region echo, Ny fix, Nz message.
  • kly3p/src/outputConverter.C: same change (the file is a verbatim copy of the Gun3P converter; a shared helper would remove the duplication but was out of scope).
  • gun3p/testsuites-new/grid-region/: README.md, run.sh, make_inputs.py, check.py.

docs.title: Follow-up
docs.text:
• ace3p-docs: add XRange, YRange, ZRange to the Outputs rows in docs/modules/gun3p/index.md and docs/reference/commands/gun3p.md. The generated keyword table in docs/reference/gun3p.md is refreshed by the docs workflow on the next release tag.
  • The magnetostatic (m) path shares the same code and keys, but was not exercised in the validation because the LSBK example has no converged magnetostatic DOFs.

docs.title: Omega3P
docs.text:
Omega3P computes the resonant modes of an RF cavity: the eigenfrequencies, the quality factors, and the electromagnetic field distribution of each mode. It is the most widely used ACE3P module and the starting point for most other analyses, since Track3P, TEM3P, and the acdtool RF post-processor all consume its output.

Cavities analyzed in the tutorials: rounded pillbox, coax coupler, waveguide coupler with lossy load, and a traveling-wave cell.

docs.title: What it solves
docs.text:
In the frequency domain, Maxwell's equations in a source-free cavity reduce to the vector wave equation for the electric field:

\[ \nabla \times \left(\mu^{-1} \nabla \times \mathbf{E}\right) - \omega^2 \varepsilon\, \mathbf{E} = 0 \]

Discretizing with high-order Nédélec vector finite elements gives a generalized eigenvalue problem \(K\mathbf{x} = \lambda M\mathbf{x}\) with \(\lambda = \omega^2\). Omega3P handles three cases:

Case Eigenvalue When Lossless, closed cavity Real Perfect electric or magnetic walls, periodic boundaries. Wall loss and Q0 are computed afterward by perturbation from the surface conductivity. Open or lossy cavity Complex Waveguide ports, absorbing boundaries, lossy dielectrics, surface impedance. The imaginary part gives the external or dielectric Q. Multiple ports with different cutoffs Nonlinear Each port adds a frequency-dependent term. Solved with the CORK rational Krylov method.

The frequency is \(f = \omega / 2\pi\) and, for a complex eigenvalue, \(Q = \mathrm{Re}(f) / 2\,\mathrm{Im}(f)\).

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Perfect electric and magnetic boundary conditions for symmetry reduction
  • Periodic boundaries with an arbitrary phase advance, for dispersion curves of traveling-wave structures
  • Waveguide ports with modal expansion, for coupler external Q
  • Absorbing boundaries for simple beam-pipe truncation
  • Volume materials with complex permittivity, for loads and windows
  • Surface conductivity for wall-loss Q0, and surface impedance for coatings
  • Finite-element orders 1 through 6 on curved tetrahedra
  • Adaptive mesh refinement driven by an error estimate
  • Checkpoint and restart of long eigensolves

docs.title: Input file
docs.text:
The input <project>.omega3p uses the common blocks plus EigenSolver and, for open cavities, one Port block per port. A complete lossless example:

pillbox.omega3p
ModelInfo : {
  File: ./pillbox4.ncdf
  BoundaryCondition : {
    Magnetic: 1, 2
    Exterior: 6
  }
  SurfaceMaterial : {
    ReferenceNumber: 6
    Sigma: 5.8e7
  }
}

FiniteElement: {
  Order:           2
  CurvedSurfaces: on
}

EigenSolver : {
  NumEigenvalues: 2
  FrequencyShift:  1.0e9
}

PostProcess : {
  Toggle: on
  ModeFile: mode
}

docs.title: EigenSolver block
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning NumEigenvalues 1 How many modes to find, counting upward in frequency from FrequencyShift FrequencyShift 10 GHz Target frequency. The solver finds the modes nearest to and above this value. Set it a little below the lowest mode you want. FrequencyShiftImag 0 Imaginary part of the shift, for complex problems Tolerance 1e-8 Relative residual for eigenpair convergence MaxIterations 200 Krylov iteration limit SolverMode automatic Choose the algorithm explicitly: Arnoldi, InexactLanczos, ESIL, SOAR, CORK. Automatic picks by problem type. CORK Sub-block with TargetFrequencyMin, TargetFrequencyMax, TargetFrequencyImag, ApproxTolerance, ApproxMaxDegree for the nonlinear solver. See Tutorial 2.

The full list, including adaptive refinement and matrix dump options, is in the Omega3P keyword reference, and every block is described key by key in the Omega3P command syntax.

When is a multi-port problem quadratic, and when nonlinear?

With waveguide ports the eigenproblem is quadratic, and the default solver handles it, when every port loads one mode and all ports share the same cutoff frequency. The CW23 slides give the example of a pillbox whose waveguide coupler and both beam-pipe ends are all declared Waveguide with one mode each. When ports have different cutoffs, or several modes per port, the problem is nonlinear and there are three options in increasing accuracy and cost: the 1D Absorbing boundary (an approximation), a PML (a good approximation, see the command syntax), or the CORK nonlinear solver (accurate but harder to converge).

docs.title: Port block
docs.text:
Port : {
  ReferenceNumber : 7     // sideset of the port surface
  NumberOfModes : 1       // waveguide modes to load at this port
}

A surface listed under Waveguide in BoundaryCondition must have a matching Port block, or Omega3P loads one mode by default. The port is treated as matched for every loaded mode. Choosing how many modes to load is discussed in Tutorial 2.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
srun -n 16 omega3p <project>.omega3p

Omega3P is a pure MPI program; use one rank per core. Results go to omega3p_results/ next to the input file. Start with 16 ranks on one node for meshes up to a few hundred thousand elements and add nodes when the memory report in omega3p.out passes about 70 % per node. System-specific batch scripts are in Batch jobs.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Results go into omega3p_results/ next to the input file.

File Content omega3p.out Full log: parsed input, mesh statistics, DOF count, iteration history, and a Mode block per eigenpair with Frequency, QualityFactor, ExternalQ, TotalEnergy, PowerLoss, and the field file name omega3p.log Shorter progress log omega3p.warn Warnings. Read this if a result is unexpected. omega3p.l0.m0000.<freq>.mod Field file for mode 0 at refinement level 0. One per mode. For complex problems the name carries R<real>.I<imag>. 2dports.log Cutoff frequencies and types of the waveguide modes computed on each port surface VECTOR/ Raw eigenvectors

A typical mode summary:

Mode : {
    TotalEnergy : 4.2137588190101e-12 , 0
    ExternalQ : 267.27097453785
    QualityFactor : 26238.857067312
    File : omega3p_results/omega3p.l0.m0000.R1.1762928e+09.I2.2005621e+06.mod
    PowerLoss : 1.1869161916105e-06
    Frequency : 1176292763.7678 , 2200562.1182804
}

QualityFactor is the wall-loss Q0 from SurfaceMaterial. ExternalQ is from the ports and is only present for complex problems. The two Frequency numbers are the real and imaginary parts in hertz.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
1. Pillbox cavity: the complete workflow from Cubit journal to R/Q, plus a mesh convergence study.
  2. Coax and waveguide couplers: waveguide ports, external Q, and the nonlinear eigenproblem with two ports.
  3. Lossy load and periodic boundaries: multiple materials with complex permittivity, and a dispersion point of a disk-loaded structure.

Post-processing with acdtool postprocess rf has its own page: Post-processing.

docs.title: Post-processing with acdtool
docs.text:
ParaView shows field patterns. For numbers such as shunt impedance, kick factor, and peak surface fields, use the RF post-processor built into acdtool:

acdtool postprocess rf <project>.rfpost

It runs serially and reads the mode files that Omega3P or S3P wrote. Running it with no file argument writes a sample.rfpost template containing every available function with default values, which is the easiest way to start.

docs.title: The .rfpost file
docs.text:
The file is a sequence of named blocks. The first must be RFField, which selects the mode and sets scaling. Every other block is a calculation that is enabled with ionoff = 1.

pillbox-rtop.rfpost
RFField
{
   ResultDir   = omega3p_results   // where the .mod files are
   FreqScanID  = 0                 // S3P only: frequency scan index
   ModeID      = 0                 // which mode, when a block uses modeID = -1
   xsymmetry   = magnetic          // [none, electric, magnetic]
   ysymmetry   = magnetic
   gradient    = 2.0e7             // V/m; -1 keeps normalized fields
   cavityBeta  = 1.0               // particle beta for V and R/Q integrals
   reversePowerFlow = 0            // [1 = charging, 0 = decaying]
   x0 = 0.0                        // integration axis x
   y0 = 0.0                        // integration axis y
   gz1 = -0.057                    // integration start z, m
   gz2 =  0.057                    // integration end z, m
   npoint = 300                    // points along the axis
   fmnx = 10                       // field map resolution
   fmny = 10
   fmnz = 50
}

RoverQ
{
   ionoff = 1
   modeID1 = -1                    // -1, -1: all modes
   modeID2 = -1
   x1 = 0.0
   x2 = 0.0
   y1 = 0.001
   y2 = 0.001
   z1 = 1e8                        // 1e8: use the model bounding box
   z2 = 1e8
}

maxFieldsOnSurface
{
   ionoff = 1
   surfaceID = 6
}

docs.title: RFField keys
docs.text: Key Meaning ResultDir Results directory from the solver ModeID Mode used by single-mode functions xsymmetry, ysymmetry Tell the post-processor which symmetry planes were used so volume integrals are scaled to the full cavity gradient Accelerating gradient in V/m used to scale fields. With -1, fields keep the solver's normalization of 1 J stored energy. cavityBeta Particle velocity for the transit-time factor in V and R/Q gz1, gz2 Axial integration range for the voltage. Set to the cavity length, not the whole beam pipe, to define the gradient consistently.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Block Computes RoverQ Voltage along a line and R/Q = V²/(ωU) per mode RoverQT Transverse R/Q kickFactor Transverse kick factor FieldMap Field on a 3D grid of nx × ny × nz points in the given box FieldAtPoint, ALLFieldAtPoint Field at one point, for one or all modes FieldOnLine, ALLFieldOnLine Field along a line with npoint samples at a given rfphase, written to filename fieldOn2DBoundary Field on a boundary surface, written to file fieldOnSurface Field on a surface as components or amplitude maxFieldsOnSurface Peak E and H on a surface with their locations Multipole analysis Multipole decomposition of the field on axis

Coordinates are in meters. A coordinate of 1e8 means "use the bounding box of the model," which is convenient for line integrals along the full axis.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
acdtool writes to standard output and to rfpost.out. It begins with a mode summary:

** Omega3P/S3P Mode Summary:
**   Total number of modes :      2
**      ModeID         Frequency(r,i)                       Qext
**         0           1.31381e+09, 0.00000e+00           0.00000e+00
**         1           2.32914e+09, 0.00000e+00           0.00000e+00
**   Model bounding box: ( 0.00000e+00,  0.00000e+00 -1.50000e-01)
**                       ( 1.00005e-01,  1.00123e-01  1.50000e-01)

followed by a [scaling] block giving the voltage and the factor used to scale the normalized fields to the requested gradient, then one block per enabled function:

[RoverQ]
{  // RoverQ=V^2/(omega*U)
 ModeID  Frequency           (V_r, V_i)                      |V|            RoQ(ohm/cavity)
    0   1.31381e+09  ( 2.2980e+00,  3.4925e+00)    4.18073e+00      1.19567e+02
    1   2.32914e+09  (-7.2671e-04,  6.2729e-04)    9.59998e-04      3.55621e-06
}

[maxFieldsOnSurface]
{
   surfaceID :   6
      ModeID :   0
        Emax :  4.22488e+07 (V/m)   at ( 3.9627e-02,  1.8486e-02, -4.5454e-02)
        Hmax :  5.80786e+04 (A/m)   at ( 3.3116e-02,  7.9193e-02,  3.2771e-02)
}

Surface field values correspond to the gradient in RFField. The ratio Epeak/Eacc is a standard figure of merit and comes straight from Emax divided by gradient.

R/Q convention

acdtool reports R/Q in the circuit convention V²/(ωU) in ohms per cavity, where V is the full on-axis voltage after the transit-time factor. For a symmetric model the xsymmetry and ysymmetry settings restore the full-cavity stored energy. Divide by 2 for the linac convention if your comparison uses it.

docs.title: S3P results
docs.text: The same tool works on S3P output. Set FreqScanID to pick a frequency point from the scan and ModeID to pick the excited port mode.

docs.title: Tutorial 3: lossy load and periodic boundaries
docs.text: Two further Omega3P features: a second material with complex permittivity, which absorbs power and produces a complex eigenvalue without any port, and periodic boundary conditions for one cell of a traveling-wave structure.

docs.title: Part A: waveguide coupler with a lossy load
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/omega3p/pillbox+recWG+load

Instead of terminating the waveguide of Tutorial 2 with a port, fill its end with a lossy dielectric. The journal step3-ADD-load.jou webcuts the guide at y = 200 mm so the far section becomes a separate volume.

docs.title: Imprint and merge
docs.text:
Two volumes that touch must share a single interface surface, otherwise the mesh is disconnected across it and the solver sees two separate cavities. Cubit does this with imprint and merge:

reset
import acis "pillbox+recWG+load.sat"
imprint body 1 2
merge body 1 2
volume all scheme Tetmesh
volume 1 sizing function type skeleton scale 7 time_accuracy_level 2 min_size auto max_size 15 max_gradient 1.2
volume 2 sizing function type skeleton scale 7 time_accuracy_level 2 min_size auto max_size 10 max_gradient 1.2
mesh volume all

Sideset 1 surface 4 20
Sideset 2 surface 9
Sideset 6 surface all except 4 20 9 1

block 1 volume 1          # vacuum
block 2 volume 2          # load
block all element type tetra10
volume all scale 0.001
export Genesis "pillbox+recWG+load.gen" block all overwrite

Each volume goes in its own block so the solver can assign different materials. The load gets a finer mesh since the wavelength inside a high-permittivity material is shorter.

After imprint and merge, the interface between guide and load is one surface. Verify this in Cubit before export.

docs.title: Input with two materials
Results
docs.text:
Eigenvalue: (591.2395988707802, 0.1200579050951992)
        Frequency: (1160172571.152617, 117793.09714004)
Eigenvalue: (600.8495902547749, 90.41431550096833)
        Frequency: (1172850486.101091, 87749817.12126675)

Mode 0 at 1.160 GHz has a small imaginary part, Q of about 4900 from the load, and is the cavity mode. Mode 1 at 1.173 GHz has an imaginary part of 88 MHz, Q below 10, and lives mostly in the load. Heavily damped modes like this appear whenever a lossy volume is present; recognize them by their very low Q and by inspecting the field in ParaView.

docs.title: Part B: periodic boundaries for a disk-loaded structure
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/omega3p/dlwg-pbc
