docs.title: acdtool command syntax
docs.text:
acdtool is the pre- and post-processing utility shared by all ACE3P modules. It has three groups of tasks:

Group Tasks meshconvert, meshconvertdirect Cubit Genesis to ACE3P NetCDF, with statistics and checks mesh stats, check, fix, deform, warpsurface, and others postprocess rf, eigentomode, volmontomode, wake_new, wake_direct, transwake, coaxsignal, pic3pstats, pic3pconvert, track3p, project resource Slurm resource guidance

All run serially except postprocess rf and postprocess volmontomode, which can use several ranks. Every invocation writes acdtool.log in the working directory and overwrites any previous one.

docs.title: meshconvert
docs.text:
acdtool meshconvert <mesh.gen> [out.ncdf]
acdtool meshconvertdirect <mesh.gen> [out.ncdf]

Converts the Genesis mesh from Cubit to NetCDF, prints the statistics of mesh stats, runs mesh check, and, for meshconvert, repairs inverted second-order tetrahedra by straightening their edges. meshconvertdirect converts without the repair. The output defaults to the input name with .ncdf. How to read the statistics is on the mesh preparation page.

docs.title: mesh
docs.text:
acdtool mesh stats  <mesh.ncdf>                  # statistics only
acdtool mesh check  <mesh.ncdf>                  # find inverted quadratic tets
acdtool mesh fix    <in.ncdf> <out.ncdf>         # straighten their edges
acdtool mesh deform <in.ncdf> <out.ncdf> <scale> # scale a TEM3P deformed mesh for viewing
acdtool mesh warpsurface <warp.in>               # export boundary triangles for the Warp code

warpsurface reads a small input file:

File: SNS_1Cell_Closed_12K.ncdf
ExteriorBoundary: 6
WarpFile: SNS_1Cell_Closed_12K.txt

and writes the triangles of that sideset as index (v1) (v2) (v3) for constructing a metal surface in Warp.

The source also contains boundary, merge, partition, pick, rotate, scale, shuntimpedence, smooth, straighten, summodes, surfsmooth, transform, untangle, and warp, which the command reference does not describe.

docs.title: resource
docs.text:
acdtool resource <input.omega3p>

Reads an Omega3P input, estimates the problem size, and writes a Slurm batch script with a node and core count for Perlmutter. The guidance it encodes, from the 2025 release notes:

Elements (M) DOFs (M) Nodes Cores/node Time under 1 under 6 1 64 under 30 min 1 to 2 6 to 13 2 64 under 30 min 2 to 4 13 to 25 4 32 under 30 min 4 to 5 25 to 32 6 32 under 30 min 5 to 6 32 to 38 10 8 under 60 min 6 to 7 38 to 44 20 8 under 60 min

This is for Omega3P with the MUMPS direct solver at order 2. Fewer cores per node on the larger problems reflects memory per rank as the limit.

docs.title: postprocess rf
docs.text:
acdtool postprocess rf <input.rfpost>
acdtool postprocess rf                 # writes sample.rfpost with every function

Computes RF quantities from an Omega3P or S3P mode. The input is a sequence of blocks; RFField must come first and every other block is a function enabled with ionoff = 1. The Omega3P post-processing page walks through a typical file; this section lists every function.

docs.title: RFField
docs.text:
RFField {
   ResultDir   = omega3p_results
   FreqScanID  = 0            // S3P only: scan point
   ModeID      = 0
   xsymmetry   = none         // none, electric, magnetic
   ysymmetry   = none
   gradient    = 2.00000e+07  // V/m; -1 for no scaling
   cavityBeta  = 1.00000
   reversePowerFlow = 0       // 1 charging, 0 decaying, for open ports
   x0 = 0.0  y0 = 0.0         // gradient integration line
   gz1 = -0.035  gz2 = 0.035
   npoint = 300
   fmnx = 10  fmny = 10  fmnz = 50   // localizer grid for tracking functions
}

ModeID for Omega3P is the eigenmode index; for S3P it indexes the port modes in the order the ports appear in the input. gz1 or gz2 above 10⁶ means the domain limit. xsymmetry and ysymmetry restore full-cavity stored energy for a symmetric model.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
All take ionoff. Coordinates in m; a coordinate above 10⁶ means the domain limit. modeID1 = modeID2 = -1 means all modes. Functions marked "RFField mode only" act on the single mode selected in RFField.

Block Computes Keys beyond ionoff RoverQ R/Q = V²/(ωU) per mode, ohm per cavity modeID1, modeID2, line x1 y1 z1 to x2 y2 z2 RoverQT Transverse RT/Q modeID1, modeID2, offset x0 y0, z1, z2 RoverQRoverQT R/Q and RT/Q in both planes at once modeID1, modeID2, radial offset r0, z1, z2 kickFactor Transverse kick factor as RoverQT pointRoverQ E²/(ωU) at a point, for power needed to reach a field there modeID1, modeID2, x0 y0 z0 dFSlater Frequency shift from a surface error by Slater perturbation modeID1, modeID2, derror (m, positive reduces RF volume), box x1 x2 y1 y2 z1 z2 VFFT Multipole components of the on-axis voltage printGroup (nterm or ModeID), modeID1, modeID2, nterm, ntheta (power of 2), r0, z1, z2 GBZFFT Multipole components of momentum change for a particle; RFField mode only filename, nterm, ntheta, energy (eV), npoint, r0, z1, z2, phase1, phase2, nphase Multipole Dipole and quadrupole terms of the momentum change, simplified; RFField mode only as GBZFFT without nterm, ntheta FieldMap E and B on a regular grid to Efield-map.dat, Bfield-map.dat; RFField mode only nx ny nz, x1 x2 y1 y2 z1 z2 IMPACTMap Same grid in IMPACT format to EBfield-map-<filename>.dat as FieldMap plus filename, rot180 OpenPMD_IMPACT Same grid as OpenPMD HDF5: E_Real.h5, E_Imag.h5, B_Real.h5, B_Imag.h5 as FieldMap FieldAtPoint E and B at a point; RFField mode only x0 y0 z0 ALLFieldAtPoint At a point for a range of modes modeID1, modeID2, x0 y0 z0 FieldOnLine Along a line at a phase, scaled to gradient; RFField mode only. Writes <filename>.e, .b at the phase and .ec, .bc complex. npoint, filename, rfphase, line endpoints ALLFieldOnLine Along a line for a range of modes, in the solver's normalization as FieldOnLine plus modeID1, modeID2, rot180 fieldOn2DBoundary E and B on the x = 0 trace of a surface; RFField mode only filename, surfaceID fieldOnSurface E and B on a surface; RFField mode only filename, surfaceID, output (amplitude or component) maxFieldsOnSurface Peak E and H on a surface with locations; RFField mode only surfaceID powerThroughSurface Complex Poynting flux through a surface, W; RFField mode only surfaceID

docs.title: eigentomode and volmontomode
docs.text:
acdtool postprocess eigentomode  <jobname>     # omega3p_results or s3p_results
acdtool postprocess volmontomode <jobname>     # t3p_results

Regenerate .mod files from stored eigenvectors or volume-monitor .out files. The solvers do this automatically unless PostProcess.Toggle is off or the job ran out of time before the conversion.

docs.title: wake_new, wake_direct, transwake
docs.text:
acdtool postprocess wake_new    <jobname> <x y>
acdtool postprocess wake_direct <jobname> <x y>
acdtool postprocess transwake   <jobname> <x1 y1> <x2 y2>

wake_new recomputes the longitudinal wake at another transverse position by indirect integration; wake_direct does the same with direct integration for runs whose WakeField monitor had a Grid block. transwake applies the Panofsky-Wenzel theorem to the longitudinal wakes at two transverse points to produce the transverse wake and kick factor; it works only with indirect integration. All three rewrite <jobname>/OUTPUT/wakefield.out. Because the Laplace extension is mesh-based, the wake is evaluated at the mesh point nearest the requested coordinates, which are reported in the file header; choosing coordinates on the mesh avoids the offset.

docs.title: coaxsignal
docs.text:
acdtool postprocess coaxsignal <jobname>

Combines a Power monitor named port and a ModeVoltage monitor named modecoeff on the same 50 ohm coaxial port into OUTPUT/signal.out with columns time, voltage, beam current. See the BPM tutorial.

docs.title: pic3pstats and pic3pconvert
docs.text:
acdtool postprocess pic3pstats   <particles.ncdf> <symmetry> [fwhm]
acdtool postprocess pic3pconvert <file.ncdf | file.txt>

pic3pstats prints moments and emittances of a phase-space dump unfolded by the symmetry factor, 1 or 4; with a FWHM argument it also writes slice statistics. pic3pconvert converts between the NetCDF dump and a text table of x px y py z pz, in either direction depending on the extension.

docs.title: track3p
docs.text:
acdtool postprocess track3p <input.acdtool> [jobname]

EnhancementCounter : {
   Token              : on
   SEYFileName1       : copper.dat
   SEYFileName2       : niobium.dat
   BoundarySurfaceID1 : 6
   BoundarySurfaceID2 : 3
   SolidVolID         : 0
   MinimumEC          : 0.01
   OutputFile         : en
}
Trajectory : {
   Token      : on
   ParticleID : 2300 7011
}

EnhancementCounter recomputes EC from the stored impact data with the given SEY files, so one tracking run can be evaluated for several surface treatments. Trajectory writes each listed particle's path as a text file named by its ID.

docs.title: project
docs.text:
acdtool postprocess project <eigenmodes path> [displacements path]

Projects a TEM3P static or harmonic displacement field onto a set of TEM3P mechanical eigenmodes by L2 inner product over the mesh, which must be identical in both runs. Without the second argument it projects the eigenmodes onto themselves as an orthogonality check. Results go to standard output and acdtool.log.

docs.title: Gun3P command syntax
docs.text:
Block-by-block description of the .gun3p input file. The Gun3P module guide explains the iteration and the sheet beam gun example.

Top-level blocks: DCGunProblem, ElectrostaticProblem, MagnetostaticProblem, Tracker.

docs.title: DCGunProblem
docs.text:
DCGunProblem : {
  RunId:          test
  SymmetryFactor: 1                        // 1 full, 2 half, 4 quarter
  // JustGenerateTreecotree: On
  ElectricAbsoluteTolerance:  0.
  ElectricRelativeTolerance:  1.00e-12
  ElectricAbsoluteTolerance2: 0.
  ElectricRelativeTolerance2: 1.00e-12
  MagneticAbsoluteTolerance:  0.
  MagneticRelativeTolerance:  1.00e-12
  MaxIterations: 32
  // FirstIterationForMagnetostaticProblem: 1
  Save iteration data: On
}
Key Meaning RunId Run label SymmetryFactor Scales emitted current to the full gun JustGenerateTreecotree Run on one core to build the tree-cotree gauge for the magnetostatic solve; needed if that solve does not converge. Does not create output. ElectricRelativeTolerance Convergence on the E-field change between iterations with the magnetic solver off ElectricRelativeTolerance2, MagneticRelativeTolerance The same with the magnetic solver on ...AbsoluteTolerance Always 0 MaxIterations Hard stop FirstIterationForMagnetostaticProblem Iteration at which the beam's self-magnetic field is first included. Commented out means never. Save iteration data Keep per-iteration fields and particles under OUTPUT/ITER_<n>/

docs.title: ElectrostaticProblem
docs.text:
ElectrostaticProblem : {
  AnodeBoundaryId: 12
  MeshFile:        dcgun.ncdf
  BasisOrder:      2
  CurvedSurfaces:  on
  Charge averaging factor: 0.1

  VolumeMaterial : {
    Id:         1
    MediumName: Vacuum
    PhysicalParameter : { Name: Permittivity  ConstantValue: 1. }
  }

  Write dofs to disk:     on
  Debug bd dofs mapping:  Off
  Debug matrix assembly:  Off
  Use reduced solver:     On

  Outputs : {
    Dofs for vizualization: On
    ElectrostaticFieldToken: On          // export on a Cartesian grid for Track3P
    FileName: test.data
    Nx: 40  Ny: 50  Nz: 60
    XRange: -0.02 0.02                   // optional, metres; default: mesh bounding box
    YRange: -0.01 0.01
    ZRange:  0.0  0.10
  }

  Boundary : { Id: 1   ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 0. }
  Boundary : { Id: 2   ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: -500. }
  Boundary : { Id: 3   ConditionType: Neumann    NeumannValue: 0. }
  Boundary : { Id: 12  ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 115000. }

  Compute non zero initial guess: On
  LinearSolver : {
    Solver:            CG                // CG for large, MUMPSFLOAT for small problems
    Preconditioner:    CHOLESKY
    PrintFrequency:    50
    QuietMode:         0
    AbsoluteTolerance: 1.00e-99
    Tolerance:         1.00e-16
    MaxIterations:     5000
  }
}
Key Meaning AnodeBoundaryId Anode sideset MeshFile, BasisOrder, CurvedSurfaces As in TEM3P Charge averaging factor Under-relaxation: new = (1 − f) × previous + f × computed VolumeMaterial.PhysicalParameter Name is Permittivity, Permeability, or Sigma; ConstantValue its value Write dofs to disk Save the field for the output converter Use reduced solver Eliminate constrained DOFs; keep on Debug ... Developer output; keep off Outputs.Dofs for vizualization Needed for gun3pOutputConverter Outputs.ElectrostaticFieldToken, FileName, Nx, Ny, Nz Also write E on a structured grid, for ElectroStaticFieldMap in Track3P Outputs.XRange, YRange, ZRange Optional. Two values each, min max in metres, setting the grid extent per axis. Omitted axes use the mesh bounding box. Exactly two values are required and min must be below max. Boundary Dirichlet fixes the potential in V; Neumann fixes the normal derivative, usually 0 on symmetry and open boundaries Compute non zero initial guess Warm-start each iteration from the previous solution LinearSolver Keep as shown

docs.title: MagnetostaticProblem
docs.text: Same structure as ElectrostaticProblem with all Boundary blocks Dirichlet 0. The examples keep Name: Permittivity in the material, which the code accepts. Solver: MUMPSFLOAT is typical.

      Whole boundary is emitter: On

      Forward velocity factor: 1.
      Min allowed distance: 0.01e-3

      Max allowed emission distance wrt z axis: 1.000000
      First inter cycle factor: 1.0
      Inter cycle averaging factor: 1.0
      Max allowed total current: 1.35e+9     // μA

    }

}
Key Meaning JobName Output path; agree with the second command-line argument t Forward tracking duration. Long enough for the slowest particles to reach the screen. Backward Backward tracking from the emission reference plane to the cathode, used to set launch conditions Domain.Emission N*, Tracking N* Localizer grid resolution in the emission and tracking regions Domain.Tracking box Region outside which particles are dropped Monitor.PlaneCrossingsVsT One plane; reports emittances and, with Compute densities, current density on a grid of X number by Y number cells out to Max x and Max y Monitor.PlanesCrossing A stack: First plane point, Common plane normal, Distance between first and last planes, Number of planes MeshInterface Localizer; keep as shown Emitter.Type 6 for Child-Langmuir, the usual gun model. docs.title: gun3pOutputConverter
docs.text:
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p e [iter]     # electric field
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p m [iter]     # magnetic field

Converts the stored DOFs of the final iteration, or of iteration iter, into OUTPUT/E/staticDofs.ncdf.mod or OUTPUT/M/... for ParaView, and writes the Cartesian-grid field file when ElectrostaticFieldToken was on.

docs.title: Omega3P command syntax
docs.text:
Block-by-block description of the .omega3p input file. Each block is shown as a complete example followed by the meaning of every key. Narrative explanations and worked cases are in the Omega3P module guide; the machine-generated list of every keyword the code reads, with defaults and source locations, is in the Omega3P keyword table.

Top-level blocks: ModelInfo, FiniteElement, PRegion, EigenSolver, Port, PostProcess.

docs.title: ModelInfo
docs.text:
ModelInfo : {
  File: ./pillbox+recWG4.ncdf
  BoundaryCondition : {
    Magnetic:  1, 2
    Electric:  3, 4
    Exterior:  6
    Waveguide: 7
  }
  SurfaceMaterial : {
    ReferenceNumber: 6
    Sigma: 5.8e7
  }
  Material : {
    Attribute: 1
    Epsilon:   1.0
    Mu:        1.0
  }
}

File: mesh in NetCDF format, with an optional path. Default directory is where the job was submitted.

BoundaryCondition: maps boundary types to the sideset numbers assigned in Cubit. Every surface must belong to exactly one.

Type Meaning Electric Tangential E = 0. Perfect conductor or electric symmetry plane. Magnetic Tangential H = 0. Magnetic symmetry plane. Exterior Computationally identical to Electric, but marks a real metal wall so that wall loss and Q0 are computed by perturbation using the conductivity in SurfaceMaterial. Impedance Fields related by a surface impedance from the conductivity in SurfaceMaterial. For a lossy conductor when the skin depth is small compared with the element size. Requires FrequencyShift to be close to the mode frequency, since the impedance is evaluated there. Absorbing First-order absorbing boundary for waves at c. For coaxial ports and beam pipe truncation. See Port with CutoffFrequency. Waveguide Modal waveguide boundary. Pair with a Port block. Periodic_M, Periodic_S Master and slave surfaces of a periodic boundary. Their surface meshes must be identical. Theta Phase advance in degrees between master and slave.

SurfaceMaterial: wall properties for loss calculation. ReferenceNumber is the sideset; Sigma the conductivity in S/m. Absent, the wall is copper at 5.8×10⁷ S/m. Repeat the block for surfaces of different materials.

Material: volume properties by Cubit block. Absent, the volume is vacuum.

Key Meaning Attribute Block ID Epsilon, Mu Relative permittivity and permeability EpsilonImag, MuImag Imaginary parts for material loss. Default 0. Negative for a passive lossy material. PML Sub-block making this block a perfectly matched layer, below

docs.title: PML
docs.text:
A perfectly matched layer terminates a domain by absorbing outgoing waves in an artificially lossy region. The conductivity ramps from zero at the inner face to a maximum at the outer face:

where \(d\) is the layer thickness, \(m\) the polynomial order, \(R\) the desired reflection coefficient, and \(\eta_0\) the free-space impedance. Give either Reflection Coefficient, from which the maximum is computed, or Maximum Sigma directly.

Free-space termination needs face, edge, and corner layers; a waveguide termination needs one face layer.

Material : {
  Attribute: 2
  PML: {
    Type: Face
    Start: -0.01143 -0.00508 0.08       // bounding box of the layer, m
    End:    0.01143  0.00508 0.10
    Direction: 0. 0. +1.                // outward normal
    Reflection Coefficient: 1.e-5
    Polynomial Order: 2
    Maximum Sigma: 2.e0 2.e0 2.e0       // alternative to Reflection Coefficient
  }
}
Key Meaning Type Face (6 orientations), Edge (12), or Corner (8) Start, End Bounding box of the layer in m Direction Orientation: one nonzero component for Face, two for Edge, three for Corner, each ±1 Reflection Coefficient Target reflection; sets Maximum Sigma Maximum Sigma Conductivity in x, y, z in S/m, if not derived from the reflection coefficient Polynomial Order \(m\) in the profile

A spherical or cylindrical PML replaces the bounding box and direction with the layer geometry:

PML: {
  Type: Face
  SubType: Sphere            // or Cylinder
  BoundaryID: 6              // sideset of the outer surface
  Radius: 0.05
  Thickness: 0.004
  Reflection Coefficient: 1.e-5
  Polynomial Order: 2
}

docs.title: FiniteElement
docs.text:
FiniteElement : {
  Order:          2
  CurvedSurfaces: on
}

Order is the polynomial order of the basis functions, 1 to 6; 2 is adequate for most work. CurvedSurfaces (also accepted as Curved Surfaces) uses the mid-edge nodes of the quadratic mesh to represent curved boundaries; default on.

docs.title: PRegion
docs.text:
Different orders in different blocks. Set the global order to 0 and give each block its own:

FiniteElement : { Order: 0  CurvedSurfaces: on }
PRegion : { Type: Material  Reference: 1  Order: 2 }
PRegion : { Type: Material  Reference: 2  Order: 3 }

Reference is the block ID. Every block must then appear in a PRegion.

docs.title: EigenSolver
docs.text:
EigenSolver : {
  NumEigenvalues: 1
  FrequencyShift: 1.0e9
  Tolerance:      1e-7
  MaxIterations:  300
}
Key Default Meaning NumEigenvalues 1 Modes to find, counting upward from FrequencyShift FrequencyShift 10 GHz Modes above this frequency are searched. Set just below the lowest mode of interest. Tolerance 1e-8 Relative eigenpair residual MaxIterations 200 Krylov iteration limit

The default solver handles real (lossless) and complex (lossy or port-loaded) problems as linear or quadratic eigenproblems. A port-loaded problem stays quadratic only when every loaded port mode shares the same cutoff frequency. Otherwise use the nonlinear solver below.

docs.title: Linear solver inside the eigensolver
docs.text:
The shift-invert operator inside each Arnoldi iteration can use PETSc instead of the default direct solver, which matters for problems too large for MUMPS:

EigenSolver : {
  NumEigenvalues: 1
  FrequencyShift: 1.0e9
  Arnoldi: {
    LinearSolver: {
      Solver: PETSc
      Preconditioner: MP         // p-order multilevel preconditioner
      SubCommSize: 8
      Tolerance: 1e-10
      MaxIterations: 8000
      PETScOption: {
        Runtime: -ksp_type cg -log_view -options_left -ksp_converged_reason
      }
    }
  }
}
Key Default Meaning Solver MUMPS PETSc to use a PETSc Krylov solver Preconditioner PETSc built-in MP: ACE3P's multilevel preconditioner, which solves at order 1 to precondition order 2 SubCommSize 8 MPI sub-communicator size for MP Tolerance 1e-16 Relative convergence MaxIterations 1000 Krylov iteration cap PETScOption.Runtime PETSc command-line options; several Runtime lines allowed

Use -ksp_type cg for lossless (Hermitian) problems and -ksp_type gmres for lossy (non-Hermitian) ones; CG diverges on the latter. Complex problems need the binaries built against complex PETSc, in the bin-petsc-complex directory of the installation. The same LinearSolver nesting applies inside ESIL, InvertMode, and the other eigensolver containers.

docs.title: Nonlinear eigensolver (CORK)
docs.text:
EigenSolver : {
  NumEigenvalues: 3
  Tolerance:      1e-10
  FrequencyShift: 1.0e9
  SolverMode:     CORK
  CORK: {
    TargetFrequencyMin:  1.0e9
    TargetFrequencyMax:  2.4e9
    TargetFrequencyImag: 5.0e8
    MaxIterations:       500
    ApproxTolerance:     1e-12
    ApproxMaxDegree:     100
    OneRKSShift:         1
  }
}
Key Meaning TargetFrequencyMin, TargetFrequencyMax Real-frequency search window in Hz TargetFrequencyImag Largest imaginary part searched, Hz MaxIterations Nonlinear iteration cap ApproxTolerance Accuracy of the rational approximation ApproxMaxDegree Maximum polynomial degree of the approximation OneRKSShift Use a single rational Krylov shift. Read by CORK_RationalNewton.C; present in the CW23 example but not described in the command reference.

Procedure: run once loading many modes per port, read the cutoffs in 2dports.log, count the propagating modes at each port for the modes of interest, and rerun loading only those. Tutorial 2 walks through it.

docs.title: Port
docs.text:
Port : {
  ReferenceNumber: 7
  NumberOfModes:   1
}

One block per Waveguide surface. Absent, one mode is loaded. ReferenceNumber must match the sideset listed under Waveguide.

For an Absorbing surface, a Port block with CutoffFrequency improves the first-order boundary by giving it the guide's phase velocity at the eigenfrequency instead of c:

Port : {
  ReferenceNumber: 7
  CutoffFrequency: 1e9
}

docs.title: PostProcess
docs.text:
PostProcess : {
  Toggle:    on
  ModeFile:  mode
  WriteLoss: on
}
Key Default Meaning Toggle on Write .mod field files for ParaView ModeFile omega3p Prefix of the mode files WriteLoss off Also write .loss files with the surface power density distribution. Read as PostProcess.WriteLoss in the shared post-processor emfem/src/NewPP.C.

Post-processing of modes for R/Q, kick factors, and field extraction is done by acdtool postprocess rf; see the acdtool command syntax.

docs.title: Pic3P command syntax
docs.text:
Block-by-block description of a .pic3p input, which is run by the t3p executable. The Pic3P module guide explains the physics and the LCLS gun example.

Top-level blocks: ModelInfo, FiniteElement, PRegion, Loading, TimeStepping, Monitor, LinearSolver, CheckPoint.

docs.title: ModelInfo, FiniteElement, TimeStepping, LinearSolver, CheckPoint
docs.text: As in T3P. Boundary types used in PIC: Electric, Magnetic, Exterior, Absorbing (beam entry and exit, coax), Waveguide.

docs.title: PRegion
docs.text:
The causal moving window:

FiniteElement : { Order: 0  CurvedSurfaces: on }
PRegion : { Type: PICCausality  Order: 1 }
PRegion : { Type: PICDomain     Order: 1 }

PICCausality is the region reachable from the particles within the light cone; PICDomain is the sub-region enclosing the particles themselves and may take a higher order, with 2 or above recommended for accuracy. Outside both, the order is 0.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
Loading : {
  SymmetryFactor: 4
  SymmetryOrigin: 0 0 0

  Particles : {
    TrackingOnly: no
    z0:           -6.0325e-2
    TotalCharge:  -1e-9
    Distribution : {
      Beta:              0 0 0.003
      NumberOfParticles: 1e3
      Radial :       { rMin: 0  rMax: 1e-3 }
      Longitudinal : { Type: Flattop  DeltaT: 10e-12  RiseTime: 2e-12 }
    }
    Monitors : {
      DumpInterval:            2e-11
      DumpPhases:              18 64
      DumpPositions:           0 1e-2
      ObserverPlaneZPositions: -2e-2 2e-2
    }
  }

  ConstantField : { E: 0 0 0  B: 0 0 0 }

  DriveField : {
    FieldValueAtPhase0:       -120e6
    FieldComponent:           2
    SamplePoint:              0,0,-6.0325e-2
    CentroidPhaseBeforeCrest: -58
    Omega3PMap : { Directory: omega3p_results  ModeNumber: 1 }
  }
}
Key Meaning SymmetryFactor 2 for half, 4 for quarter model SymmetryOrigin Point the symmetry planes pass through, m

docs.title: Particles
docs.text:
Key Meaning TrackingOnly yes disables space charge z0 Injection plane, m TotalCharge C; negative for electrons Distribution Built-in generator or File Monitors Phase-space output control, below

Built-in distribution: Beta (initial v/c vector), NumberOfParticles, Radial with rMin and rMax (uniform), Longitudinal with:

Type Keys Flattop DeltaT duration, RiseTime for each edge, both in s Gaussian SigmaT, NumSigma Ellipsoid DeltaT

File distribution: Distribution : { File: dist.ncdf }. Create the file from a text table whose first line is the particle count and each following line is x px y py z pz in m and normalized momentum, converted with acdtool postprocess pic3pconvert dist.txt.

Self-consistent emission instead of Distribution:

Block Keys FieldEmission BoundaryID, Work Function (eV), FieldEnhancement, MaxCurrentDensity (A/m²) ThermionicEmission BoundaryID, A, B for J = A exp(B √E), MaxCurrentDensity DCEmission BoundaryID, BeamCurrentDensity (A/m²), Beta0

Monitors:

Key Meaning DumpInterval Phase-space dump every this many seconds DumpPhases Dump at these drive-field phases, degrees DumpPositions Dump when the bunch centroid reaches these z, m ObserverPlaneZPositions Record every particle crossing of these z planes

Output goes to <jobname>/OUTPUT/Particles/.

docs.title: ConstantField
docs.text: Uniform external E in V/m and B in T.

docs.title: DriveField
docs.text:
The RF field. Several DriveField blocks may be given.

Key Meaning FieldValueAtPhase0 Field at RF phase zero at SamplePoint, V/m. Sign convention follows TotalCharge. FieldComponent 0, 1, 2 for x, y, z SamplePoint Normalization point, m CentroidPhaseBeforeCrest Injection phase of the bunch centroid, degrees before crest Omega3PMap Directory and ModeNumber (from 0) PoissonMap File and Frequency for a Superfish map instead

A Solenoid block with SolenoidStrength (T), Component, SamplePoint, and a PoissonMap adds a static focusing field.

docs.title: Monitor
docs.text: Point and Volume monitors as in T3P; WakeField is available but rarely used in PIC. See the T3P command syntax.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: See the module guide for the particle files and the columns of particles.stat. Post-processing with acdtool postprocess pic3pconvert and pic3pstats is in the acdtool command syntax.

docs.title: S3P command syntax
docs.text:
Block-by-block description of the .s3p input file. Worked cases are in the S3P module guide.

Top-level blocks: ModelInfo, FiniteElement, FrequencyScan (or WaveguideFrequency), Port, Loading, LinearSolver, PostProcess.

docs.title: ModelInfo
docs.text:
Identical in form to Omega3P's, including Material with EpsilonImag and MuImag, PML, and SurfaceMaterial. Boundary types available: Electric, Magnetic, Exterior, Impedance, Absorbing, Waveguide. Periodic boundaries are not available in S3P.

Two extensions to SurfaceMaterial matter in S3P:

SurfaceMaterial : {
  ReferenceNumber: 3
  Sigma:     5.8e7
  Frequency: 5e9                 // frequency at which Sigma applies
  Coating : {
    Type:      ThinLossyDielectric
    Epsilon:   56
    Sigma:     12
    Thickness: 1.e-3
  }
}

Frequency fixes the frequency at which the surface impedance is evaluated for an Impedance boundary. Coating adds a thin lossy dielectric layer on the conductor without meshing it; see the T3P surface impedance tutorial for the physics.

docs.title: FiniteElement
docs.text: As in Omega3P: Order 1 to 6 and CurvedSurfaces.

docs.title: FrequencyScan
docs.text:
FrequencyScan : {
  Start:    9.424e+9
  End:      14.424e+9
  Interval: 0.2e+9
}

Frequencies in Hz. If Interval exceeds End − Start, only Start is computed. For a single frequency the shorthand WaveguideFrequency: 1.3e+9 at top level is equivalent.

docs.title: Port
docs.text:
Port : {
  ReferenceNumber: 7
  NumberOfModes:   2
}

One per Waveguide surface; absent, one mode is loaded. Load every mode that propagates anywhere in the scan range.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
Dipole excitation as an alternative to port excitation, for mode identification:

Loading : {
  Type:       DipoleLoading
  Coordinate: 0., 2., 0.         // m
  Direction:  0.0, 1.0, 0.0
  Tolerance:  0.001
  Power:      1.                 // dipole moment, A·m
  Frequency:  30.e3              // Hz
}

Tolerance sets how closely the dipole direction must align with the nearest element edge.

docs.title: LinearSolver
docs.text:
The default is the MUMPS direct solver. For large problems use an iterative solver with the multilevel preconditioner, which requires Order: 2:

LinearSolver : {
  Solver:         GMRES          // MUMPS, GMRES, CG, QMR
  Preconditioner: MP
  MaxIterations:  5000
  Tolerance:      1e-10
  PrintFrequency: 50
  QuietMode:      0              // 1 suppresses iteration output
}

MP first solves at order 1 with MUMPS to build a preconditioner, then iterates at order 2. The 2025 release notes give a resource table for this configuration on Perlmutter: 7 million elements on 4 nodes in 10 minutes, 47 million on 32 nodes in 2 hours.

PETSc solvers are also available with the same Solver: PETSc and PETScOption syntax as in Omega3P. Use -ksp_type cg only for lossless problems and -ksp_type gmres for lossy ones; complex problems need the bin-petsc-complex binaries.

docs.title: PostProcess
docs.text:
PostProcess : {
  Toggle:     on
  PortNumber: 7                  // save fields only for this excitation port
  ModeFile:   rec                // default s3p
  WriteLoss:  on
}

Without PortNumber, fields are written for every port excitation at every frequency, which multiplies the output. WriteLoss is read by the shared post-processor in emfem/src/NewPP.C and writes .loss surface power density files.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text: See the S3P module guide for Reflection.out, 2dports.log, and the per-mode port files. acdtool's rf post-processor reads S3P results with FreqScanID selecting the scan point; see the acdtool command syntax.

docs.title: T3P command syntax
docs.text:
Block-by-block description of the .t3p input file. Worked cases are in the T3P module guide.

Top-level blocks: ModelInfo, FiniteElement, PRegion, LoadingInfo, Loading, TimeStepping, Monitor, LinearSolver, CheckPoint.

docs.title: ModelInfo
docs.text:
As in Omega3P with these differences.

Boundary types: Electric, Magnetic, Exterior, Absorbing, Waveguide (broadband, dispersive), Impedance.

Material gains time-domain options:

Material : {
  Attribute: 1
  Epsilon:   35.83
  Mu:        1.0
  Sigma:     0.316           // bulk conductivity, S/m, frequency independent
  Chi2:      ...             // second-order nonlinear susceptibility
  Chi3:      ...             // third-order nonlinear susceptibility
  Dispersion : {             // Lorentz model; only one dispersive material allowed
    Type:    Lorentz
    Omega_0: ...             // resonance angular frequency
    Omega_p: ...             // resonant strength
    Gamma:   ...             // decay rate
    Eps_inf: ...             // high-frequency permittivity
  }
}

The Lorentz permittivity is

\[ \varepsilon(\omega) = \varepsilon_\infty + \frac{\omega_p^2}{\omega_0^2 - \omega^2 + j\omega\gamma} \]

SurfaceMaterial takes Frequency and an optional Coating as in S3P. The Impedance boundary with a SurfaceMaterial is also what the SurfacePowerLoss monitor reads.

PML is as in Omega3P, with Polynomial Order typically 3 in time domain.

docs.title: FiniteElement and PRegion
docs.text:
Order and CurvedSurfaces as elsewhere. For the moving window, set the global order to 0 and define the window:

FiniteElement : { Order: 0  CurvedSurfaces: on }
PRegion : {
  Type:         AutomaticMovingWindow
  Order:        2
  Back:         0.001          // m behind the bunch
  Front:        0.002          // m ahead
  StructureEnd: 0.0689         // z where the window stops moving
}

The window spans Back plus the bunch length plus Front. When the bunch reaches the front of the window a new window is created and the system matrix is reassembled, so a very short window saves per-step cost but adds reassembly cost. The wake is valid only up to about Back behind the bunch.

docs.title: LoadingInfo
docs.text:
Beam excitation by a rigid bunch moving at c along z.

LoadingInfo : {
  Bunch : {
    Type:             Gaussian
    Sigma:            0.01            // m
    Number of sigmas: 5
    Charge:           1e-12           // C
  }
  SymmetryFactor:  4.0
  StartPoint:      0 0 -0.10
  Direction:       0 0 1
  BoundaryID:      3
  StartTime:       1.e-9              // optional, s
  NumBunches:      2                  // optional, bunch train
  BunchSeparation: 0.1                // optional, m
}

Bunch shapes:

Type Keys Gaussian Sigma, Number of sigmas (or Nsigmas). Total length 2 × Sigma × Number of sigmas. BiGaussian Sigma1 (front), Sigma2 (back), Number of sigmas. Asymmetric. Flattop Rise sigma, Number of rise sigma, Drop sigma, Number of drop sigma, Flattop width. Half-Gaussian edges on a flat top. Key Meaning SymmetryFactor 2 if the beam lies on one magnetic symmetry plane, 4 at the corner of two. Scales the effective charge in the domain. StartPoint, Direction Entry point and direction; only z is allowed BoundaryID Surface the beam enters through; make it Absorbing StartTime Injection time of this bunch, default 0 NumBunches, BunchSeparation A train of identical bunches spaced in m

Several LoadingInfo blocks give several independent bunches, used for dipole excitation with opposite charges.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
Dipole, port, and surface excitation.

DipoleLoadingPortModeLoadingSurfaceLoading 
Loading : {
  Type:       DipoleLoading
  Coordinate: 0.0001, 0.00001, 0.
  Direction:  0.0, 0.0, 1.0
  Tolerance:  0.001
  Excitation : {
    Power: 1.                        // dipole moment, A·m
    Pulse : { ... }                  // see Pulse below
  }
}

Loading : {
  Type: PortModeLoading
  Port : {
    ReferenceNumber: 3
    SymmetricFactor: 4               // 1 none, 2 one plane, 4 two planes
    NumberOfModes:   1
  }
  Excitation : { Power: 1.  Pulse : { ... } }
}

The port surface is Absorbing in ModelInfo so outgoing waves leave. Port modes are solved numerically, or imported from files:

Port : {
  ReferenceNumber: 3
  Origin:     0.0 0.0 -1.928
  XDirection: 1.0 0.0 0.0
  YDirection: 0.0 1.0 0.0
  ESolver : {
    Type: Interpolative
    Mode : { ExFile: Ex.prn  EyFile: Ey.prn  BxFile: Bx.prn  ByFile: By.prn }
  }
}

Each file is a table of ix iy x y F on an M×N grid, rows advancing ix fastest, E in V/m and B in T.

Loading : {
  Type:            SurfaceLoading
  ReferenceNumber: 4
  InputFile:       TM01.prn
  Excitation : { Mode number: 1  Power: 1.  Pulse : { ... } }
}

A user field map on a curved Absorbing surface, given on a (θ, φ) grid as ix iy theta phi Ex Ey Ez Bx By Bz, angles in radians.

docs.title: Pulse
docs.text:
Type Keys Gaussian Frequency (carrier, Hz), Bandwidth (Hz), DB (truncation below peak), T0 (delay in sigmas), Phase (degrees) Monochromatic Frequency, Rise periods (cycles to full amplitude), Fall periods (optional), T0 (start time, s), TMax (total duration, s, optional) UserDefinedPulse T0 (time offset, s), Scaling, Frequency (for port-mode evaluation, Hz), File: two-column text, time and amplitude

Note that SymmetricFactor inside Loading.Port is spelled differently from SymmetryFactor in LoadingInfo. Both are as the code reads them.

docs.title: TimeStepping
docs.text:
TimeStepping : {
  MaximumTime: 3.0e-9
  DT:          1e-12
}

Both in seconds. The implicit scheme is unconditionally stable, so DT is set by the frequency content to be resolved.

docs.title: Monitor
docs.text: Type Keys Output Point Name, Coordinate <Name>.out: t, Hx Hy Hz, Ex Ey Ez in SI Volume Name, TimeStart, TimeEnd, TimeStep <Name>ts_t<time>ps.out.mod snapshots for ParaView WakeField Name, StartContour, EndContour, Smax, optional Grid <Name>.out: s, W(s) in V/C, I(s) in A/m, with loss or kick factor in the header Power Name, ReferenceNumber, optional TimeStart, TimeEnd, TimeStep <Name>.out: t, power through the surface in W SurfacePowerLoss Name, ReferenceNumber <Name>.out: t, ohmic loss on the surface in W. Needs a SurfaceMaterial on that surface. ModeVoltage Name, Port with ReferenceNumber and ESolver (Type: Numerical2D, NumberOfModes, Frequency, Tolerance, MaxIterations) <Name>.out: t, modal voltage in V

docs.title: WakeField details
docs.text:
StartContour and EndContour bound the integration in z and default to the model ends. Smax is the wake length recorded and is limited by causality: with model length L and downstream pipe length l, the maximum is c × MaximumTime − (L − l).

The default is indirect (Weiland) integration along the beam-pipe boundary, valid when only vacuum is visible from pipe end to pipe end. The wake is computed at the beam's transverse position; for other positions use acdtool postprocess wake_new, and for transverse wakes acdtool postprocess transwake.

For collimator-like structures with intrusions, use direct integration along a circle inside the vacuum:

Monitor : {
  Type: WakeField
  Name: wakefield
  StartContour: 0.
  EndContour:   0.6
  Smax:         0.10
  Grid : {
    Method:     Circle
    Radius:     0.0149       // m
    NPoints:    10
    StartDense: 0            // degrees
    EndDense:   90
    Fraction:   1
  }
}

A long downstream catch-up distance is needed for convergence. acdtool postprocess wake_direct evaluates it at other positions.

docs.title: LinearSolver
docs.text:
LinearSolver : { Solver: MUMPS }
LinearSolver : { Solver: CG  Preconditioner: CHOLESKY }

MUMPS, direct, for small problems. CG with CHOLESKY or DIAGONAL for large ones. A missing or misspelled Solver key gives the compiled-in default, MUMPS on the SLAC and NERSC builds.

docs.title: CheckPoint
docs.text:
CheckPoint : {
  Action:     restart        // none or restart; restart is default
  Ntimesteps: 700            // interval, default 1000
}

Resubmitting a run with restart continues from the last checkpoint. To extend a finished run, raise MaximumTime and resubmit.

docs.title: TEM3P command syntax
docs.text:
Block-by-block description of the .tem3p input file. Worked cases are in the TEM3P module guide.

Problem blocks: ThermostaticProblem, ElasticProblem, ThermoElasticProblem. Within a problem: MeshFile, BasisOrder, CurvedSurfaces, solver blocks, materials, Shell, HeatSource, Boundary, MeshDump, EigenSolver, HarmonicAnalysis, Transient.

docs.title: Problem types
docs.text:
ThermostaticProblem : { ... }       // steady-state thermal, linear or nonlinear

ElasticProblem : { ... }            // static elasticity, eigenmodes, or harmonic response

ThermoElasticProblem : { RunId: 3 } // marker: run the following thermal then elastic
ThermostaticProblem : { ... }       // problems in sequence, passing temperature
ElasticProblem : { ... }

Each problem block begins with the mesh:

MeshFile:       RfGunBody.ncdf
BasisOrder:     2
CurvedSurfaces: on

docs.title: Solvers
docs.text:
LinearSolver : {
  Solver:            CG            // CG, GMRES, MUMPS
  Verify:            yes           // compute the residual; default no
  SaveDOFs:          yes           // keep DOFs for post-processing; default yes
  Preconditioner:    DIAGONAL      // DIAGONAL, CHOLESKY, SSOR, ILU
  AbsoluteTolerance: 1.0e-18
  Tolerance:         1.0e-10
  MaxIterations:     100000
}

PicardSolver : { ... same keys ... }      // used for Picard steps in nonlinear solves

NonlinearSolver : {
  Solver:          Newton
  PicardIteration: 10              // Picard steps before switching to Newton
  MaxIterations:   40
  AbsTolerance:    2.33e-10
  RelTolerance:    1.0e-8
}

EigenSolver : {                    // in ElasticProblem: mechanical eigenmodes
  NumEigenvalues: 5
  FrequencyShift: 1.0              // Hz
}

HarmonicAnalysis : {               // in ElasticProblem: forced response
  Start:    50                     // Hz, scan
  End:      250
  Interval: 50
  Frequency: 50                    // single frequency instead of a scan
  StiffnessDamping: 0.01           // Rayleigh damping coefficients
  MassDamping:      100000
}

Picard iteration first, then Newton, stabilizes nonlinear thermal solves. The eigensolver needs homogeneous boundary conditions and Density in the material. Harmonic analysis treats Neumann loads as amplitudes at each frequency; with damping the system is complex and the linear solver must handle it.

Note

AbsoluteTolerance inside LinearSolver is from the command reference. The example inputs spell it AbsoluteTolerante, and neither string is read by tem3p/src/LinearSolverMan.C, which reads Tolerance (default 1e-10). The only absolute tolerances the code reads are ThermalAbsoluteTolerance and ElasticAbsoluteTolerance in ThermoElasticProblem.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
ThermalConductivity : { Id: 1  Value: 391 }                  // W/(m·K)
ThermalConductivity : { Id: 3  Function: functions/ss304 }   // k(T) from a file

VolumeMaterial : {
  Id: 1
  ElasticLambda: 8.1244e+10        // Pa; or give
  ElasticMu:     4.3363e+10        // Pa
  // YoungsModulus: 17e6           // Pa, with
  // PoissonsRatio: 0.36
  ElasticAlpha:  1.70000e-5        // 1/K; not used by the eigensolver
  Density:       8960              // kg/m³; eigensolver only
}

Id is the Cubit block. Either the Lamé pair or Young's modulus with Poisson's ratio may be given; the conversion is \(\mu = E/2(1+\sigma)\) and \(\lambda = E\sigma/(1+\sigma)(1-2\sigma)\).

docs.title: Function files
docs.text:
A nonlinear property is a text file of piecewise expressions in T:

Tstart   Tend     f(T)
-1000.0  2.8322   2.8800
2.8322   2.9743   3.0832*T+(-5.8522)
...

Used by ThermalConductivity.Function, Boundary.SurfaceResistance, Boundary.RobinFactor, and Boundary.RobinValue.

docs.title: Shell
docs.text:
Shell : {
  Bd:         6                    // sideset carrying the shell
  Material:   221                  // a ThermalConductivity Id
  BasisOrder: 1
  Thickness:  1e-5                 // m
}
ThermalConductivity : { Id: 221  Function: functions/CURRR100 }

A thin conducting layer on a surface, for platings and coatings, without meshing it. Material refers to a ThermalConductivity block, not a mesh block.

docs.title: HeatSource
docs.text:
Volumetric heating, two kinds:

HeatSource : {                     // dielectric loss from an RF field
  Id:                  5           // block
  ConditionType:       RFHeating
  WhichMode:           0
  DielectricConstantE: 9
  LossTangentE:        0.0001
  Directory:           s3p_results
  Method:              Powerinput
  TargetPowerinput:    437.5       // W
}

HeatSource : {                     // external heating map, FLUKA format
  Id:              9
  ConditionType:   ExtVHeating
  ExtVHeatingFile: heating_file.dat
}

The FLUKA file has six header lines, then r1 r2 nr dr, theta1 theta2 ntheta dtheta, z1 z2 nz dz, a power scaling factor, a dummy line, and nr × ntheta × nz power densities with r varying fastest.

docs.title: Thermal Boundary
docs.text:
Boundary : { Id: 2  ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 2 }          // K
Boundary : { Id: 4  ConditionType: Neumann    NeumannValue: 0. }           // W/m² into the surface
Boundary : {
  Id: 5
  ConditionType: Robin                                                       // convection
  RobinConstantFactor: 20000.0                                               // h, W/(m²·K)
  RobinConstantValue:  440000.0                                              // h × T_ambient
}
Boundary : {
  Id: 5
  ConditionType: Robin
  RobinFactor: functions/He2p2f                                              // nonlinear h(T)
  RobinValue:  functions/He2p2v
}

docs.title: RFHeating
docs.text:
Heat flux from a field solution. Four ways to scale it:

Powerinput (S3P)Gradient (Omega3P)PowerLossRFHeatingMap 
Boundary : {
  Id: 8
  ConditionType:     RFHeating
  WhichMode:         0
  Directory:         s3p_results
  Method:            Powerinput
  TargetPowerinput:  437.5             // W
  SurfaceResistance: functions/SRinnerCU
}

Boundary : {
  Id: 6
  ConditionType:  RFHeating
  WhichMode:      0
  Sigma:          5.8e7
  Directory:      omega3p_results
  Method:         Gradient
  TargetGradient: 60e6                 // V/m
  DutyFactor:     0.00036
  StartPoint:     0.0001, 0.0001, -0.017018
  EndPoint:       0.0001, 0.0001,  0.017018
}

Boundary : {
  Id: 6
  ConditionType:   RFHeating
  WhichMode:       0
  Directory:       omega3p_results
  Method:          PowerLoss
  TargetPowerloss: 500                 // W total on metal
  Sigma:           5.8e7
}

Boundary : {
  Id: 6
  ConditionType: RFHeatingMap
  InputFile:     power.txt             // ix iy theta phi F, W/m²
}
Key Meaning WhichMode Mode index, from 0 Directory Field solver results Method Powerinput, Gradient, or PowerLoss TargetPowerinput, TargetGradient, TargetPowerloss The target in W, V/m, or W StartPoint, EndPoint Gradient integration line, m Sigma Conductivity for computing loss from the surface H, S/m SurfaceResistance Function file Rs(T) instead of Sigma DutyFactor Multiplies the load for pulsed operation SymmetryFactor Reference says 1 full, 0 half for heating; 0 full, 1 half, 2 quarter for detuning. Inconsistent in the reference document. EMHeating.C reads it with default 0 and a warning when absent; check tem3p.out for the value applied.

docs.title: Mechanical Boundary
docs.text:
Boundary : { Id: 1  ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 0. }         // all components fixed, m
Boundary : { Id: 4  ConditionType: Neumann    NeumannValue: 0. }           // normal traction, Pa; positive pushes into the surface
Boundary : {
  Id: 2
  ConditionType: Mixed
  MixedType:  DIRICHLET NEUMANN NEUMANN                                      // per direction x y z
  MixedValue: 0., 0., 0.
}

docs.title: LFDetuning
docs.text:
Radiation pressure from a field solution:

Boundary : {
  Id:             6
  ConditionType:  LFDetuning
  WhichMode:      0
  Directory:      omega3p_results
  Omega3PId:      6                       // wall sideset in the vacuum mesh
  Method:         Gradient                // Gradient, Voltage, or Powerinput
  TargetGradient: 60e6
  GradientDirection: 0, 0, 1              // default
  SymmetryFactor: 2
  StartPoint:     0.0001, 0.0001, -0.017018
  EndPoint:       0.0001, 0.0001,  0.017018
}

Method: Voltage takes TargetVoltage in V and VoltageDirection; Method: Powerinput takes TargetPowerinput in W.

docs.title: MeshDump
docs.text:
MeshDump : {
  WriteDeformedMesh:   on          // body mesh with displacements
  WriteDeformedEMMesh: on          // vacuum mesh with mapped displacements
  MeshDeformScale:     1.0         // multiply displacements; for mode shapes
  EMMeshInputDir:      omega3p_results
  WriteStressStrain:   on
}

docs.title: Transient
docs.text:
Time-dependent thermal analysis inside ThermostaticProblem:

Transient : {
  TimeStepping : {
    Type:        Thermal
    Scheme:      BackwardEuler
    MaximumTime: 8.e1              // s
    DT:          4.e-1
    InitialT:    0.                // start time
    InitialTemp: 25.               // °C
  }
  Excitation : {
    Power: 1.
    Pulse : {
      Type:         Monochromatic
      Frequency:    1.
      Rise periods: 10
      T0:           0.
    }
  }
}

The Excitation block reuses T3P's pulse machinery to modulate the heat load in time; Fall periods and TMax are optional as in T3P.

docs.title: Post-processing
docs.text: acdtool mesh deform exaggerates a deformed mesh for viewing, and acdtool postprocess project decomposes a static or harmonic displacement field onto a set of mechanical eigenmodes. See the acdtool command syntax.

docs.title: Track3P command syntax
docs.text:
Block-by-block description of the .track3p input file. Worked cases are in the Track3P module guide.

Top-level: TotalTime, ParticlesTrajectories, FieldScales, NormalizedField, Emitter, Domain, Material, OutputImpacts, SingleParticleTrajectory, Postprocess. The mesh and fields come from the solver results named in Domain; there is no ModelInfo.

docs.title: TotalTime
docs.text:
TotalTime: 50

Tracking duration in RF cycles. Default 20.

docs.title: ParticlesTrajectories
docs.text:
ParticlesTrajectories : {
  ParticleFile: partpath
  Start: 0
  Stop:  1000000
  Skip:  1
}

Controls PARTICLES/partpath_ts*.ncdf output. Only active when ScanToken is 0. Start, Stop, Skip are in time steps.

docs.title: FieldScales
docs.text:
FieldScales : {
  Type:      FieldGradient
  ScanToken: 1
  Minimum:   23.0e+6
  Maximum:   25.0e+6
  Interval:  1.0e+6
  Scale:     23.00e+6          // used when ScanToken is 0
}
Key Meaning Type FieldGradient (V/m, averaged along the NormalizedField line), InputPortPower (W, for S3P fields), StorEnergy (J) ScanToken 1 scans Minimum to Maximum by Interval, no trajectory files; 0 runs the single level Scale and writes trajectories

docs.title: NormalizedField
docs.text:
NormalizedField : {
  Beta:       1
  StartPoint: 0.0 0.0 -0.057
  EndPoint:   0.0 0.0  0.057
  N:          300
}

The line along which the accelerating voltage is integrated for Type: FieldGradient. N points, default 300; Beta for the transit-time factor, default 1.

docs.title: Emitter
docs.text:
Emitter : {
  Type:          2
  t0: 0   t1: 1                // emission window in RF cycles
  x0: -0.03  x1: 0.035         // bounding box, m
  y0:  0.04  y1: 0.1
  z0: -0.045 z1: 0.0
  BoundaryID:    6
  SkipTimeSteps: 1
  N:             1000          // field emission only
  WorkFunction:  4.2           // eV, field emission only
  Beta:          120           // enhancement, field emission only
}

Several Emitter blocks may be defined.

Type Name Meaning 2 ElectronicSurface Default. Primaries from the mesh surface inside the box. 5 SolidElectronicSurface From mesh surfaces and from boundaries between material regions; for RF windows. Needs SolidRegion and VacuumRegion in Domain. 7 FieldEmission Fowler-Nordheim, for dark current. N is the minimum electrons per emitted macroparticle; WorkFunction default 4.2 eV (copper); Beta the field enhancement factor. 10 ParticlesFile Load particles from a text file named by ParticlesFile: one line per particle with electron count, energy in eV, x y z in m, and momentum components. Optional XScale, YScale, ZScale, EnergyScale, XOffset, YOffset, ZOffset.

Other numbered types exist in the shared emitter code (1 ThermalCathode, 3 Injector, 4 EmitterSamples, 6 ChildLangmuir, 8 PICInput, 9 PlaneFieldEmission); 6 is the model Gun3P uses.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
Domain : {
  FieldDir:        ./omega3p_results
  ModeID:          0
  FrequencyScanID: 0             // S3P only
  dt:              1
  MaxImpacts:      50
  LowEnergy:       20
  HighEnergy:      5000
  InitialEnergy:   2.0
  Voltage:         0.0 0.0 0.0
  Bins:            64
  SolidRegion:     2             // RF windows
  VacuumRegion:    1
  ExternalMagneticField: 0.0 0.0 4.0
  MagneticFieldMap : { File: bfield2  Scaling: 0.0001  Units: 0.001  ZOffset: 0.27 }
  ElectroStaticFieldMap : { File: ./gun3p_results/OUTPUT/E/test-11.txt  Scaling: 1.0 }
  SymmetryFactor:  2
  SymmetryPlane:   5
}
Key Default Meaning FieldDir Omega3P or S3P results directory ModeID 0 Eigenmode index (Omega3P) or port-mode index (S3P). The source also accepts ModeID1. FrequencyScanID 0 Scan point in an S3P result dt 1.0 Time step = dt / frequency / 100 MaxImpacts 50 Particles die after this many impacts LowEnergy, HighEnergy 5, 1e9 eV Impact energy window outside which no secondaries are emitted InitialEnergy 2 eV Launch energy Voltage 0 0 0 DC coax bias as a ra rb: V = a / ln(rb / ra), units V m m Bins 64 Localizer bins along the longest axis; the others derive from it SolidRegion, VacuumRegion Block IDs for window problems ExternalMagneticField 0 0 0 Uniform B in T MagneticFieldMap Cylindrically symmetric map in Poisson text format: header lines r0 rN Nr and z0 zN Nz, then Fr Fz [Fphi] rows with r varying fastest. Scaling multiplies the field, Units converts the coordinates to m, ZOffset shifts the origin. ElectroStaticFieldMap Cartesian-grid field from gun3pOutputConverter; File, Scaling SymmetryFactor, SymmetryPlane 1, none Model symmetry and the sideset of the symmetry plane, used with a SymmetryPlane material

docs.title: Material
docs.text:
Material : { Type: Primary    BoundarySurfaceID: 6 }
Material : { Type: Secondary  BoundarySurfaceID: 3 4 6 }
Material : { Type: Absorber   BoundarySurfaceID: 7 8 }
Material : { Type: SymmetryPlane  BoundarySurfaceID: 5 }

Material : { Type: Primary    SolidBlockID: 2 }        // RF window dielectric
Material : { Type: Secondary  SolidBlockID: 2 }

Material : {
  Type: Secondary
  BoundarySurfaceID: 6
  Model: 2
  SecondaryEmissionYield: sey.dat
  MinimumNumElectrons: 1000
  ElasticThreshold:    1000
}
Type Behavior Primary Primaries may launch here Secondary Impacts emit secondaries per Model Absorber Impacts kill the particle SymmetryPlane Specular reflection

BoundarySurfaceID is a sideset list; SolidBlockID a block, for window dielectrics.

Model Secondary emission 1 (default) Multipacting: one secondary per impact, emitted normal to the surface 2 Dark current: true secondaries and elastically reflected particles at random angles, following a yield table from SecondaryEmissionYield (two columns, energy in eV and yield) or inline Sigma0 and Einit lists. MinimumNumElectrons and ElasticThreshold prune small macroparticles. 3 Furman-Pivi model with multiple secondaries per impact. MAT_SecondaryEmitter.C branches on model 3; the parameters it reads are not in the command reference.

docs.title: OutputImpacts and SingleParticleTrajectory
docs.text:
OutputImpacts:            on      // default off; writes ImpactsInfo_<level>
SingleParticleTrajectory: off     // default off; on writes one file per particle named by ID

docs.title: Postprocess
docs.text:
Postprocess : {
  Toggle: on
  ResonantParticles : {
    Token:          on
    InitialImpacts: 4
    EnergyRange:    25 10000
    PhaseTolerance: 0.01
  }
  EnhancementCounter : {
    Token:              on
    SEYFileName1:       copper.txt
    BoundarySurfaceID1: 6
    SEYFileName2:       niobium.txt
    BoundarySurfaceID2: 3
    SolidVolID:         0
    MinimumEC:          0.01
  }
}

ResonantParticles flags trajectories that repeat in phase. InitialImpacts (default 4) is the minimum impact count considered; EnergyRange in eV discards impacts outside it; PhaseTolerance is the phase match criterion.

EnhancementCounter computes EC = δ1 δ2 … δm over a particle's impacts, with δi the SEY at the i-th impact energy from the file for that surface. Two surfaces with different materials can be given. SolidVolID names a window volume. MinimumEC (default 10) suppresses rows below it.

The same counter can be recomputed after the run with a different SEY file by acdtool postprocess track3p; see the acdtool command syntax.

docs.title: ACE3P v2026.11
docs.text:
From the ACE3P source tree

Written by the ACE3P developers in docs/user/CHANGES/next.md and copied here for release v2026.11 on 2026-10-28. Propose changes in the ACE3P repository, not on this page.

docs.title: Track3P
docs.text:
• Step loop up to 15x faster on large meshes with identical results: Domain.Bins omitted (or <= 0) now picks about one element per bin along the longest axis instead of 64, and particle localization starts from the previous element and its face neighbours before the grid. Inputs that carry Bins: 256 should drop that line. KEK 56-cell field emission, 30 RF cycles, one node: 1794 s to 122 s. (PR #239)
  • Startup: DOF numbering skipped for tracking, field-emission faces owned per rank instead of sampled on every rank, one shared vertex-field pass for InterpolationMethod: Linear. The loop timing report is always printed on rank 0. See the Track3P page "Faster particle localization and startup".

docs.title: Gun3P
docs.text: • gun3pOutputConverter (and kly3pOutputConverter): the structured-grid E-field export accepts optional XRange, YRange, ZRange in Outputs to set the grid extent per axis; omitted axes keep the mesh bounding box. Fixes the Ny default being written to nx. See the Gun3P page "Structured-grid E-field export on a user-chosen region". (PR #240)

docs.title: Workflow overview
docs.text:
Getting started covers accounts, logging in and submitting a first job. This chapter is about what happens between a drawing and a plot: every ACE3P simulation follows the same five steps regardless of which solver you use.

flowchart LR
    A["1. Model<br/>Cubit journal"] --> B["2. Mesh<br/>Cubit, export .gen"]
    B --> C["3. Convert<br/>acdtool meshconvert<br/>.gen to .ncdf"]
    C --> D["4. Solve<br/>omega3p, s3p, t3p, ..."]
    D --> E["5. Post-process<br/>ParaView, acdtool postprocess"]
Step Tool Where Input Output 1. Build the model Cubit HPC desktop (ThinLinc) or laptop .jou journal .sat ACIS geometry 2. Mesh the model Cubit HPC desktop or laptop .sat, .jou .gen Genesis mesh 3. Convert the mesh acdtool meshconvert HPC batch .gen .ncdf NetCDF mesh 4. Run the solver omega3p, s3p, ... HPC batch .ncdf plus <name>.<module> input results directory with .mod fields and .out log 5. Post-process ParaView, acdtool postprocess rf HPC desktop or laptop .ncdf, .mod, .rfpost plots, R/Q, surface fields

Cubit and ParaView are installed on Perlmutter and S3DF, so steps 1, 2 and 5 can be done in a ThinLinc desktop without copying files. If you run them on your own computer instead, transfer .gen files up and .mod files down with scp.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
File naming. The solver input file is named <project>.<module>, for example pillbox.omega3p or coupler.s3p. Post-processing input for acdtool is <project>.rfpost.

Boundary and material IDs. In Cubit, surfaces are grouped into sidesets and volumes into blocks. The sideset number becomes the boundary ReferenceNumber in the ACE3P input, and the block number becomes the material Attribute. Pick a consistent scheme and stick to it. The tutorials use:

Sideset Meaning 1, 2 Symmetry planes 3, 4 Beam pipe ends or additional symmetry planes 6 Exterior cavity wall 7 and up Waveguide or coax ports

Units. ACE3P expects meters. Build in millimeters if that is convenient, then volume all scale 0.001 before export.

Symmetry. Cut the model along symmetry planes to reduce the problem size. A quarter model with two magnetic symmetry planes gives the monopole modes of a cylindrically symmetric cavity. Switching one plane to electric selects dipole modes.

docs.text:

docs.title: Batch jobs
docs.text: ACE3P solvers are MPI programs and run under Slurm. The structure of a batch script is the same on every system; only the partition, account, and binary path change.

docs.title: Anatomy of a script
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH <resource and queue options>
#SBATCH -J <job name>
#SBATCH -o <stdout file>
#SBATCH -e <stderr file>

<load ACE3P environment>
srun -n <ranks> <solver> <project>.<module>

System-specific headers are in Running on S3DF and Running on Perlmutter.

docs.title: Choosing resources
docs.text:
Omega3P and S3P are memory-bound sparse eigenvalue and linear solves. Start with 16 MPI ranks on one node for meshes up to a few hundred thousand elements. Add nodes when the solver reports high memory use per node in its .out file:

used mem per node in GB : min:   4.97 GB, max:   4.97 GB, avg:   4.97 GB
used mem per node in %  : min:   40.7  %, max:   40.7  %, avg:   40.7  %

Keep the percentage under about 70 to leave room for the direct solver's fill-in.

Track3P parallelizes over particles and is OpenMP-parallel within each rank. Because every rank holds the whole mesh and field, run it in hybrid mode: one or two MPI ranks per node and OpenMP threads across the rest of the cores. Scripts are in Hybrid MPI and OpenMP below.

T3P scales to many nodes for large time-domain problems. Rank count should be proportional to element count; a rule of thumb is 5,000 to 20,000 elements per rank.

acdtool is serial. Run it with -n 1.

docs.title: Hybrid MPI and OpenMP (Track3P)
docs.text:
Track3P is the only ACE3P solver that uses OpenMP threads. The layout below puts two ranks on each node and lets threads fill the cores: 2 x 60 threads on an S3DF milano node (128 cores, 8 left for the system), 2 x 64 on a Perlmutter CPU node (128 cores). OMP_PROC_BIND=spread and OMP_PLACES=cores pin the threads so they do not migrate between sockets. The second argument to track3p is the results directory.

S3DFPerlmutter run-track3p-hybrid.sh
#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH -p milano
#SBATCH -A rfar:regular
#SBATCH -q normal
#SBATCH -N 1
#SBATCH --exclusive
#SBATCH -t 02:00:00
#SBATCH -J track3p-omp
#SBATCH -o track3p_omp_%j.log
#SBATCH -e track3p_omp_%j.log

source /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/ace3p.sh

RANKS_PER_NODE=2
NTHREADS=60
TOTAL_RANKS=$((SLURM_JOB_NUM_NODES * RANKS_PER_NODE))

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=${NTHREADS}
export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread
export OMP_PLACES=cores

srun --overlap --cpu-bind=none -n ${TOTAL_RANKS} --ntasks-per-node=${RANKS_PER_NODE} -c ${NTHREADS} \
     track3p Pillbox.track3p track3p_results
run-track3p-hybrid.batch
#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH -C cpu
#SBATCH -q regular
#SBATCH -A m349
#SBATCH -N 1
#SBATCH --exclusive
#SBATCH -t 02:00:00
#SBATCH -J track3p-omp
#SBATCH -o track3p_omp_%j.log
#SBATCH -e track3p_omp_%j.log

RANKS_PER_NODE=2
NTHREADS=64
TOTAL_RANKS=$((SLURM_JOB_NUM_NODES * RANKS_PER_NODE))

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=${NTHREADS}
export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread
export OMP_PLACES=cores

srun -n ${TOTAL_RANKS} --ntasks-per-node=${RANKS_PER_NODE} -c ${NTHREADS} --cpu-bind=cores \
     $CFS/ace3p/perlmutter/CPU/track3p Pillbox.track3p track3p_results

Raise -N for more nodes; the rank count scales with it. Add ranks rather than threads only when one rank's share of the particles takes too long, keeping the per-node memory of the replicated mesh in mind. For a quick test, one rank with 16 threads is enough:

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=16
srun -n 1 -c 16 track3p Pillbox.track3p

The end of track3p.log prints a function-by-function timing report (emission, push, material interaction) that shows whether more threads would help.

docs.title: Walltime
docs.text:
Problem Typical time Omega3P, 2 modes, 15k elements, order 2 1 to 2 minutes Omega3P, 10 modes, 500k elements, order 2 30 to 60 minutes S3P, 20 frequency points, 100k elements 10 to 30 minutes Track3P multipacting scan, 30 field levels 10 minutes to several hours depending on particle count

Use a short debug queue for the first run of a new model and check the .out file before committing to a long queue.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Each solver writes into a results directory next to the input file, omega3p_results/ for Omega3P and similar for the others. Common files:

File Content <module>.out Full log including parsed input, mesh statistics, convergence history, and the mode summary <module>.log Shorter progress log <module>.warn Warnings only. Check this first when results look wrong. *.mod Field files for ParaView, one per mode or time step VECTOR/ Raw eigenvectors for restart or post-processing

The Slurm .out and .err files capture the same console output plus any MPI runtime messages.

docs.title: Chaining steps
docs.text: A full campaign chains mesh conversion, several solves, and post-processing, often across many parameter values. Writing that as a sequence of hand-submitted scripts is error prone. The ACE3P GUI has a workflow-orchestration mode for parameter sweeps and optimization chains, and lume-ace3p does the same from Python.

docs.title: Input file format
docs.text: All ACE3P solvers read a plain-text input file with nested blocks of Key: value pairs. The file is named <project>.<module>.

docs.title: Syntax
ModelInfo
docs.text:
Describes the mesh and the physical boundary conditions.

Key Meaning File Path to the .ncdf mesh BoundaryCondition Maps boundary types to sideset IDs. See below. Material Volume material by block Attribute. Default is vacuum. Repeat for several materials. SurfaceMaterial Surface conductivity Sigma on a boundary ReferenceNumber, used for wall loss and Q0

Boundary condition types:

Type Physics Typical use Electric Tangential E = 0, perfect electric conductor Metal walls when wall loss is not needed, electric symmetry plane Magnetic Tangential H = 0 Magnetic symmetry plane Exterior Metal wall with finite conductivity from SurfaceMaterial Cavity wall when Q0 is wanted Waveguide Port surface; modal expansion with Port blocks Couplers, beam pipe ends Absorbing Simple first-order absorbing boundary Beam pipe ends when modal accuracy is not needed Periodic_M, Periodic_S Master and slave periodic surfaces with phase advance Theta in degrees Traveling-wave structures Impedance Surface impedance boundary Thin coatings, lossy surfaces

docs.title: Material
docs.text:
Material : {
  Attribute: 2          // Cubit block ID
  Epsilon: 10.0         // relative permittivity
  EpsilonImag: -1.52    // negative imaginary part for loss
  Mu: 1.0               // relative permeability
}

docs.title: FiniteElement
docs.text: Key Meaning Order Polynomial order of the vector basis functions, 1 to 6. Order 2 is the usual choice. Higher order gives more accuracy per element at higher cost. CurvedSurfaces on to use the quadratic mid-edge nodes of tetra10 elements for curved geometry. Keep this on.

docs.title: PostProcess
docs.text: Key Meaning Toggle on writes field files for ParaView ModeFile Prefix for the .mod files in the results directory

docs.title: Module-specific blocks
docs.text: Each solver adds its own blocks: EigenSolver and Port for Omega3P, SParameter and frequency scan settings for S3P, time-stepping and excitation for T3P, emission and tracking parameters for Track3P. These are documented in the module guides.

docs.title: Echo of parsed input
docs.text: Every solver prints the parsed input, with defaults filled in, near the top of its .out file under the heading input parameters, KVC syntax. Compare that echo against your file when a keyword seems to be ignored. A misspelled keyword is silently dropped, so the echo is the quickest way to catch typos.

docs.title: Mesh preparation
docs.text: ACE3P reads meshes in its own NetCDF format (.ncdf). You produce them by exporting a Genesis file (.gen) from Cubit and converting it with acdtool. Building and meshing the model in Cubit is covered on the Cubit page; this page covers what the exported mesh must contain and how to check it.

docs.title: Cubit export checklist
docs.text:
A typical meshing journal ends like this:

step2-Mesh-pillbox.jou
reset
import acis "pillbox4.sat"

volume all scheme Tetmesh
volume all sizing function type skeleton scale 5 time_accuracy_level 2 min_size auto max_size 12 max_gradient 1.2
mesh volume all

Sideset 1 surface 7                      # symmetry plane
Sideset 2 surface 1                      # symmetry plane
Sideset 6 surface all except 7 1         # exterior wall

block 1 volume all
block 1 element type tetra10             # quadratic tets, required

volume all scale 0.001                   # mm to m
export Genesis "pillbox4.gen" block all overwrite

Check each item before export:

  • Tetrahedral mesh with the Tetmesh scheme. Hex meshes are not supported.
  • Element type tetra10 on every block. Linear tetra4 elements lose the curved-surface information.
  • Every boundary surface in a sideset. Surfaces that belong to no sideset get boundary ID 0 and are treated as interior, which is almost never what you want. The idiom Sideset 6 surface all except ... catches everything you did not name explicitly.
  • Every volume in a block. Blocks become material attributes.
  • Scaled to meters.
  • Multiple volumes imprinted and merged so shared faces are a single surface. Otherwise the volumes are disconnected in the mesh. See the lossy load tutorial.

docs.title: Sizing function
docs.text:
The skeleton sizing function adapts element size to local geometry. The parameters that matter most:

Parameter Effect scale Overall density. Smaller is finer. max_size Largest edge length allowed, in model units max_gradient How fast element size may change between neighbors. 1.2 to 1.5 is typical.

Refine around small features such as coupler irises and rounded edges, and do a convergence study before trusting results. See the pillbox tutorial.

docs.title: Convert with acdtool
docs.text:
Copy the .gen file to the HPC system and run:

acdtool meshconvert pillbox4.gen

This writes pillbox4.ncdf and prints statistics. It is a serial program and finishes in seconds for meshes with fewer than a million elements, so it can run on a login node or in a one-task batch job.

docs.title: Read the statistics
docs.text:
Input: pillbox4.gen (contains quadratic 10-point elements)
Output: pillbox4.ncdf
TOTALS:
  elements: 13382
  coordinates: 2955
EULER CHARACTER:
  Surf Euler Char = 2
  Vol Euler Char = 1
  Euler Char is OK.
ASPECT RATIO:
  min      = 1.03213
  max      = 2.53273 <- GREAT
SHAPE MEASURE:
  min      = 0.26181 <- GREAT
Existing boundary IDs:
1 2 6
Material IDs     Number of Elems:
1:       13382
Total Number of invalid second order tetrahedral elements (ISOTE) is: 0

What to look for:

  • Euler characteristic OK. A closed, simply connected volume has surface Euler characteristic 2. Anything else means a hole or a disconnected piece.
  • Existing boundary IDs must match the sidesets you expect. A missing ID means a sideset was never created; an unexpected 0 means a surface was left out.
  • Material IDs must match your blocks.
  • Invalid second-order elements must be zero. A nonzero count means some mid-edge nodes fold the element inside out, usually from an aggressive sizing function on a curved surface. Refine the mesh or relax max_gradient.
  • Aspect ratio and shape measure are quality indicators. acdtool prints GREAT, GOOD, or a warning next to them. The CW23 slides give rough limits: aspect ratio above 20 or shape measure below 0.01 will slow the solvers noticeably.

docs.title: Other acdtool mesh commands
docs.text:
acdtool mesh stats pillbox4.ncdf     # statistics only
acdtool mesh check pillbox4.ncdf     # validity check only
acdtool mesh fix in.ncdf out.ncdf    # replace invalid curved tets with straight ones
acdtool mesh deform in.ncdf out.ncdf 5000   # exaggerate a deformed mesh for viewing

The full list of acdtool mesh subcommands in the current source is: boundary, check, deform, fix, merge, partition, pick, rotate, scale, shuntimpedence, smooth, stats, straighten, summodes, surfsmooth, transform, untangle, warp, warpsurface. Most are undocumented beyond their source files; meshconvert already calls check and fix for you. The full acdtool command set, including every postprocess function and the resource tool, is in the acdtool command syntax.
